Budget Compared to Actual
Final (v2)
Switch chart type
Widget size
Purpose
Answers one question at a glance: is this scope ahead of or behind its original budget, and by how many dollars? The headline is a single dollar variance with a Favourable or Unfavourable reading (type-aware: over budget is good on income, bad on expense, neutral on a mixed report line). Scope is one chip (Income accounts, Expense accounts, or a saved Special report drilled to one line), the window is one of four plain-language presets (this month, this period, this quarter, this fiscal year), and the cut is a Month/Period/Quarter/Year interval toggle. The same numbers read three ways: paired budget-and-actual bars (default), a trend line, or a sortable table; the largest size splits into two independent panels so two cuts of the same span sit side by side. Ported from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo design (its bgt block) as this widget's v2 final.
Customer Research — What We're Working Off
business_center
Bold BI — Budget vs Actual Dashboard open_in_new
A grouped bar chart (Budget vs Actual side by side, per period) is the standard first view for this exact comparison — the direct reason Variance Bar is the default view here. Bold BI's sample dashboard is the one-customer reference used for that call; Zebra BI and Domo were the separate sources used for the Waterfall alternate view and the KPI-strip placement (see Logic, below).
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

The chart compares Budget to Actual for each period of the fiscal year, as dollar amounts, so a bar sitting above or below its neighbour reads immediately as ahead of or behind plan, no subtraction required (see the 2026-07-09 fix below — this used to mislabel these dollar figures as a percentage). The KPI strip above the chart (Medium and Large only) restates the same comparison as numbers: all four figures on Large, trimmed to just Variance and % Used on Medium since there isn't room for all four without crowding the chart itself. Small drops the strip entirely and caps at 4 periods — it's a glance-sized tile, not a reporting view.

Budget-vs-actual reporting is one of the most standardised chart problems in financial dashboards, so nothing here is a novel choice: a grouped bar chart is the standard first view for this comparison, and a cumulative waterfall is the recommended second view for showing how period variances build to a year-end total — why Waterfall was kept as a full alternate view instead of being cut. Green/red variance colouring is the universal convention across every source reviewed, carried through here and in the Data Table view.

Two fixes made as part of this check: (1) the KPI header strip was previously only wired up on the Horizontal Bar List alternate view (Option B); it's now added to this default Variance Bar view's Medium/Large sizes too, matching what the locked design doc actually calls for. (2) the dedicated KPI-size card (1×0.5) was showing YTD Actual as its headline instead of the documented Variance ($), colour-coded green/red — also fixed, and now consistent with Option B's KPI card. The GL drill-through link is still pending backend confirmation — tracked separately in the developer punch list, not a gap in this widget's design.

Round 2 fixes (2026-07-09). KPI and Small card titles now read "Variance — [Account Type], [Fiscal Year]" instead of a static chart name, reusing the same generic headline function built for W02 (now extended to support more than one card size). Weekly was added as a real, selectable Period View option (previously missing from the option list entirely, despite being in the locked doc) — it's scoped to Large/Expanded in the Change Filters modal, matching the doc's "Large/Expanded only" restriction; the underlying weekly transaction-grain question is still a backend open item, unaffected by this mock-side fix.

Round 3 fixes (2026-07-09, same day). The KPI sparkline hover from Round 2 wasn't actually triggering — it used an SVG <title> child element, which doesn't reliably fire a hover tooltip on freshly-injected inline SVG here; switched to a title attribute instead, the same mechanism the grouped-bar hovers elsewhere already use successfully. The KPI-label definition bubbles from Round 2 were also getting clipped at the card's left edge for YTD Budget/Variance (the left-column labels) — they were centred on the trigger, so a narrow card had nowhere to put the left half; now anchored to the trigger's own left/right edge so they always grow inward. '% Used' (and Variance) wording was rewritten to drop the "YTD" shorthand from the explanation itself, checked against how budgeting sources plainly explain a %-of-budget figure.

Two real, confirmed bugs were also found and fixed while re-verifying the data for the above: (1) Budget/Actual per period are dollar amounts, not a percentage — the table, bar chart tooltips, and axis titles across all three views were mislabelling and displaying them as "78%" instead of "$78k"; all now show dollar amounts, with Variance additionally showing a % of that period's budget since it's the one figure that legitimately works either way. Quarterly's grouping was switched from averaging to summing months to match (averaging was only ever valid under the old, wrong %-of-budget reading). Recomputing exact sums also caught two smaller data bugs along the way: FY2026's totals didn't quite match its own periods for any Account Type (now corrected, and a partial 'Jul' period was added since FY2026 was also missing its current in-progress month entirely — that's why Quarterly could never show more than Q1+Q2 before; it now shows a real, honestly-low Q3), and Custom Report's FY2025/FY2024 totals were each exactly $100k too high, an unrelated data-entry typo. (2) This doc has always said "green = favourable (under budget on expenses / over on income)," but the KPI headline, table rows, cumulative variance, and Option B's bar chart never implemented that flip — they coloured green whenever Actual ≥ Budget regardless of Account Type, backwards for Expense Accounts/Custom Report. Now correctly flips at every level.

Every card on this page — KPI, Small, Medium, Large — is the real widget card, not a simplified stand-in: same badge, chart name/subtitle, eye (purpose) button, expand button, and 3-dot menu (download, filters, chart-type switch, size) as the live Dashboard tab. The eye and expand buttons disappear at KPI size and the chart-type switch disappears at KPI/Small — both deliberate, matching the locked size-behaviour table, not missing chrome. Size buttons here resize that card only, independent of the other three, so you can compare all four side by side; Change filters and chart-type switching are shared with the Dashboard tab's own state, since Account Type and the current view are genuinely global to Option A in the real app, not per-size. Caveat: because "Change filters" on every Final Check card size (KPI/Small/Medium/Large) delegates to the same modal the real Dashboard tab's Option A card uses, the Weekly-at-Large-only trim reads that real card's current size, not whichever Final Check card you clicked from — worth a manual check once this is wired into the real gallery.

Tried and rejected — in-widget Fiscal Year filter (2026-07-21, design call with Jo). Round 2 above added Fiscal Year as one of this widget's own filters, with its own dropdown in "Change filters" and its own slot in the KPI/Small headline ("Variance — [Account Type], [Fiscal Year]"). Rejected on review: the app already has (or will have) a page-level Fiscal Year control at the top of the page, matching the current/legacy version — giving this widget its own separate, in-widget override on top of that risked exactly the kind of "which control actually took effect" confusion this project avoids elsewhere, since a customer would have no reliable way to tell whether the page-level or widget-level value was the one actually driving the chart. Jo's call: cut the in-widget filter entirely, not rework it — Fiscal Year goes back to being page-level only, same as before this widget got its own dropdown. Account Type and Period View are unaffected; "everything else is solid" per direct instruction. Removed from the build: the Fiscal Year entry in MOCK_DATA.filters[1] (so it no longer appears in "Change filters" at any size), the 1: 'Fiscal Year' KPI-size time-filter entry (KPI size now shows no filter at all for W01, same pattern as W04/W17), and Fiscal Year's slot in the KPI/Small headline (now just "Variance — [Account Type]"). The chart itself still shows a year — fyLabel in WRENDER[1] falls back to FY 2026 exactly as it always did — there's just no widget-level way to change which year that is anymore. Kept here as history per the project's rule against deleting rejected ideas outright.

Final (v2) build (2026-07-27). Built as the v2 final from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo design (its bgt block), per direct instruction, as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[1]; the A/B/C branches above it are untouched and stay reachable from the design-option switch at the top of this section, with Final (v2) as the default. What carried over from her build: the fiscal-year data model with actual:null for unposted periods (not zero, the year is not over), eight saved special reports whose lines each carry their own account type, the type-aware favourability engine (over budget reads green on an income line, red on an expense line, and only a genuinely mixed line falls back to neutral grey), the two-purples bar chart with a per-period signed variance row on the x-axis and a formatted hover card, the trend line with its "No trend to show" guard, the sortable Period/Budget/Actual/Variance table with a "Total, posted so far" footer over posted periods only, the two-step special-report picker dialog (Report name, then Report line, Apply disabled until both are chosen), the honest no-budget empty state with a "Set up budget" action, and the shimmer skeleton on scope/span/report changes (about 850ms, reduced motion respected; interval/shape/sort re-render instantly because that data is already in hand). What this deliberately removes: the 4-tile KPI strip (YTD Budget / YTD Actual / Variance / % Used) is gone, replaced by the single KPI headline (big dollar variance plus a Favourable or Unfavourable pill and a plain-language info tooltip) and the new KPI-size glance card; the Account Type / Fiscal Year / Period View dropdowns are gone, replaced by the account-scope chip plus time-span presets plus the M/Q/P/Y interval toggle (which constrain each other: a single-period span greys out Quarter and Year and snaps the interval back to Month); the Weekly view is no longer rendered anywhere (the weekly transaction-grain question remains an open dev-feasibility item in the Step 4 doc, unaffected). No drill-through, per the composition decision. This design changed after Jo's dossier review, so this is v2 updates, not a locked final.

Sizing update (2026-07-27, same day). Small size removed for Final (v2): Jo's model has three sizes only (Glance/Detail/Explore); card proportions matched to her demo's tiers. A/B/C keep all sizes. Size terms in Final (v2) now use Jo's vocabulary: Glance (KPI size), Explore (mid), Detail (large), matching her demo's own SIZE_LABEL mapping, per General Widget Design Rules Rule 12 (corrected same day: an earlier wording had Detail and Explore reversed); A/B/C keep Small/Medium/Large.

Tweak round 1 (2026-07-27, same day). Owner decisions applied on top of the Final (v2) build. (1) The comparison window is now exactly four options, replacing Jo's span presets (owner decision): This month, This period, This quarter, This fiscal year, defaulting to This fiscal year; Last fiscal year, Last fiscal period and All time are gone from the picker. Ordering rule everywhere: period always sits before quarter, so the span picker runs month, period, quarter, fiscal year and the interval toggle now reads M P Q Y. Intervals coarser than the span grey out and snap back to Month (month span leaves only M; period and quarter spans leave M and P; the fiscal-year span allows all four), the headline caption ("vs. budget, This quarter") and the "Total, posted so far" footer follow the selected window's posted periods only, and a line with fewer than two points still falls back to Bar. (2) Glance is interactive now: its scope chip opens the same scope popover as the bigger sizes (Income accounts / Expense accounts / Special report, which opens the existing dialog) and its "vs. budget" caption opens the new span picker. (3) The headline dollar variance carries an up or down indicator and a leading sign, coloured by favourability like the table's variance column, plus a quiet percent of the window's budget (same maths as the table's variance percent), consistently at every size. (4) The line view gained a dynamic x-axis (label density computed from width and point count, so a 12-month span labels every month where it fits instead of the old fixed four ticks, with no colliding text) and a nearest-point hover readout (vertical guide plus the same Budget/Actual/Variance card the bars use; values stay in the DOM as sr-only text). (5) Explore-size crowding fixed: header, legend and slicer rows are pinned (flex-shrink 0) and layered above the plot, the wide tier gets compacted header spacing, and bar sets past the tier's comfortable width scroll horizontally instead of colliding. (6) Popover/modal bug root cause in one line: the delegated click logic was proven sound end to end in a Node reproduction of the real listeners, so the in-browser "span chip does not open" and "Special report does not work" reports trace to the compressible control rows being painted over by the chart (clicks hit the chart, never the chips) plus a stale-popover toggle path that turned the first chip click into a silent close; both fixed (rows pinned and layered per item 5, and the chip toggle now checks the popover element actually exists before treating a click as close).

Tweak round 2 (2026-07-27, same day): the Time Window Module. The comparison window grew from four options to an owner-approved five, and the whole time model is now written as a reusable module (spec: Widget_Specs/Time Window Module.md, intended for other time-series widgets too, per direct instruction). The five windows, smallest first: This month (current calendar month), This period (current fiscal period), This quarter (ROLLING: the last 3 months back from the as-of date), This year (NEW; ROLLING: the last 12 months back from the as-of date), This fiscal year (fiscal year to date; previously this window showed the full year including unposted future months, now it is strictly year to date per the approved spec). Two new grains arrived with it: Day and Week, so the interval toggle now reads D W M P Q Y (fixed order, smallest first, period before quarter). The module's law: an interval is available when it yields 2 to 31 data points for the window, plus one owner exception (Month stays available on the month and period windows as a single-pair summary); every window defaults to its SMALLEST available interval (Day, Day, Week, Month, Month respectively), and changing window snaps an invalid interval to that default. Rolling windows are anchored to an as-of date (in this mock the end of Jul 2026, implied by the current-period marker) and may cross the fiscal-year boundary, so the rolling year pulls budgets from two FYs (Aug 2025 through Jul 2026 here). Day and Week figures are deterministic synthetic data derived from the monthly mock figures: actuals spread across each posted month's days with mild seeded variation (no randomness, so renders never flicker), weeks start Monday with partial first/last weeks flagged like the partial quarter, and budgets at Day/Week grain are evenly prorated from the month. That proration is a display simplification of this mock only: the API recommendation stays a budget PACE LINE at sub-period grains, and the caveat lives in the module doc rather than the UI. Sub-period actuals are also new backend work (GLSummary is period-grain, so transaction-level querying is required); both flags are recorded in the module spec and the Step 4 doc's Sign-off Readiness table. Verified in the Node driver: bucket counts and posted totals for every window, the full constrain matrix, rolling boundaries, day-grain determinism, partial-week flags, label thinning and hover at 31 daily points, and an em-dash sweep across every window, interval, view, scope and size.

Modal fix (2026-07-27, same day). Root cause of the Special report dialog still failing in a real browser: a CSS comment above the dialog styles spelled the class prefixes as globs with a slash between them (bgt-rm-star-slash-bgt-dd-star), and the star-slash inside the first glob ended the comment early, so the leftover comment text fused into the next selector and a spec-compliant CSS parser silently dropped the entire backdrop rule (the position fixed, full-screen, z-index 3500 scrim that centres the dialog); the dialog was therefore rendering as an unstyled block at the very bottom of the page, unreachable because the modal also locks body scrolling. The Node harness passed both earlier fix rounds because it executes JavaScript against a DOM shim with no CSS parser at all, so a rule that dies in the browser's parser still "exists" as text. Fixed by rewording the comment (no star-slash sequence inside CSS comments, noted in the stylesheet itself) and, found by the same mechanical audit, re-pinning display, font-size and margin on the dialog's placeholder value spans, which this page's own global .ph rule (KPI placeholder rows) was quietly restyling. Verified three ways: a browser-faithful CSS parse check (spec comment termination plus invalid-rule error recovery) shows the backup drops exactly the backdrop rule while the fixed file drops none; the full open, choose report, choose line, preview, Apply, reopen, cancel, backdrop and Escape flow passes 34 assertions in the Node driver; and final-check-rules.py counts are unchanged. jsdom itself could not be installed here (registry blocked), so the CSS parse check stands in for it and is kept at /tmp/w01f/cssparse-check.py alongside the flow driver.

Purpose
Answers one question at a glance: how much does the conference contribute each year across every clergy pension plan, and who is on each plan? The headline is the total annual contribution with an appointee-count badge; the plans read three ways over the same filtered data (a sortable plan table with share bars, a donut of each plan's share of the total, and a grouped bar comparing plans district by district), and every row, slice and bar drills to the individual appointees on that plan, with the district filter carried through. Only active appointments count: a clergy member who is active, whose plan has started and not yet ended. This is a snapshot of what is active today, not a time series. Ported from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo pension design as this widget's Final, with the grouped bar by district added as a new view in her visual language.
Customer Research — What We're Working Off
business_center
Mercer — Plan Dashboard open_in_new
No named competitor benchmarks this exact district × plan-type combination — it's a narrower, org-specific slice than most benefits dashboards cover. Donut/pie for a proportional split is the standard choice when the question narrows to a single dimension (plan type, ignoring district) — the direct basis for Pie by Plan Type now being the default. Grouped/stacked bar charts remain the applicable standard when comparing two dimensions at once (district × plan type), which is why that chart is kept as the Switch Chart Type alternate rather than dropped.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

The default chart is a pie split by plan type — Defined Benefit, Defined Contribution, 403(b) — showing the org's overall plan mix at a glance, at every size including Small. Switching to Grouped Bar by District brings back the two-dimension view (district × plan type, stacked at Small for space, side-by-side at Medium/Large) for when the question is "who costs what," rather than "what's our plan mix." Both charts read the same Church District/Plan Type filters, so switching between them never changes what data is being looked at, only how it's drawn.

Changed on direct instruction (2026-07-09). The locked doc previously made Grouped Bar by District the default, with Donut by Plan Type as a secondary view and no Switch View at all at Small. That's been reversed here: Pie is now the default at every size, Grouped Bar is the alternate, and Switch Chart Type is now offered at Small too — all three cards above have it. The doc has been updated to match; see its Views section for the new wording.

Large now shows the chart and the Summary Table together — stacked vertically, both driven by the same filters — instead of Table being a third item in the Switch Chart Type menu. This replaces the doc's previous "Active view + table toggle" behaviour at Large with "chart and table shown together, always." Small stays chart-only. Medium now also offers a standalone Data Table via Switch Chart Type (added on direct instruction) — selecting it replaces the chart with the same District × Plan Type table Large shows, but on its own rather than paired with the chart, since Medium doesn't have the room for both at once.

Filter behaviour, corrected (2026-07-09). Selecting a specific Church District (leaving Plan Type on All Plans) narrows the pie to that one district's plan-type breakdown — this direction was already correct, confirmed by tracing the mock data, which keeps a dedicated bucket per district. Selecting a specific Plan Type, however, was a real bug: the pie used to render a single 100% slice for that one plan type instead of anything useful. It now switches the pie's slicing dimension to District — showing how that one plan is spread across Central/North/South/East/West — which is what "that plan across the district" means. Grouped Bar and the Data Table were already correct in this case (they've always broken things down by district), so only the default Pie branch needed the fix.

KPI card title now reflects the active filters (added 2026-07-09). It reads "Overall Contribution" when Church District and Plan Type are both at their "All ..." default, the district name alone when only District is narrowed, the plan type alone when only Plan Type is narrowed, and "District by Plan Type" when both are — built with a new generic function, fcKpiFilterHeadline(), rather than anything W02-specific, so the same pattern can be dropped onto another widget's KPI card later without rebuilding the truncation/tooltip/fallback logic from scratch. Long results truncate with "…" and show the full text on hover (reusing the ellipsis rule every card title already has).

One caveat: the "Switch Chart Type available at Small" change is implemented here in the WRENDER logic and on this Final Check page. The real dashboard gallery's Small-size dropdown markup for this widget lives in a large static block of HTML that this session's tooling couldn't safely inspect or edit tonight (see the review list) — worth a manual check that the same menu option appears there too.

Final build (2026-07-27). Built as the Final from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo pension widget (her pen block), per direct instruction, as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[2]; the A/B/C branches stay untouched and reachable from the design-option switch at the top of this section, with Final as the default. Purpose
Answers one question at a glance: where did payroll go for the chosen time span? The headline is the total paid out over the selected period, and the breakdown reads two ways over the same data: a sortable table (with a percent-of-total bar beside every real figure) and a donut of each slice's share. A scope chip regroups the same runs three ways without leaving the card: by distribution (the org's own payroll cost centers, such as Pastoral Staff or Facilities), by pay type (the fixed vocabulary of Regular Pay, Overtime, Housing Allowance and so on), or drilled into one distribution's own pay-type split, in place, with a context line naming the drill. The period chip carries three presets (This month, This period, This quarter) plus an always-available custom From/To date range. This is a post-payroll check of payroll already paid within the window, not a projection of what's owed. Ported from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo payroll design as this widget's Final, with the period presets aligned to the Time Window Module.

Figma Community — Free Payroll Dashboard open_in_new
Pie/donut breakdowns only work up to ~4-5 categories before bar charts become the easier read — which is why both a Bar and a Donut view are kept as peers here rather than picking one, since the right default depends on how many compensation categories a given organisation actually has. This Figma payroll dashboard is the closest reference for the horizontal-bar default; a separate source (Acciyo) is the basis for pairing the breakdown with the Period Comparison trend view, kept as a third full peer.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Current design. One row per Distribution (pay-type category — Regular, Vacation, OverTime, Sick, Double Time, Personal, Holiday, Misc, Other), sized by amount — Horizontal Bars is the default because it scales cleanly regardless of category count (Donut/Pie only reads well up to ~4-5 slices). Bar, Pie Chart and Data Table all read this exact same row set, so switching between them changes only how it's drawn, never what's being counted. Every row also shows a ▲/▼ % change against the same-length prior period (on the bar, and as a Change column on the table) — a raw total doesn't say whether costs are trending up or down, so the comparison is always visible, not tucked behind a separate view. Small shows the top 3 rows, Medium the top 5, Large all of them plus totals; the KPI headline is Total Payroll Amount for the selected period. Switch Chart Type (Bar/Pie/Table) is available at every size except KPI, including Small. (2026-07-21 update: this used to branch on a Department filter — All Departments showed one row per department with a stacked-by-Distribution bar, a specific department drilled into its own Distribution breakdown. That branch is gone; there's only ever the one breakdown now. See the tried-and-rejected note at the end of this section.)

Filters. Pay Period is Weekly/Bi-Weekly/Monthly/Custom: the three presets anchor on a Pay Date field (the date payroll is actually issued) and count backward from it — Weekly = 7 days, Bi-Weekly = 14, Monthly = 30 (a day-count approximation, not calendar-month-aware — open question, not guessed at). Custom instead reveals its own explicit Beginning/Ending date fields and ignores Pay Date entirely. A "Make this recurring" checkbox sits alongside the preset periods. The resolved end date shows above the card as "Paid: date" (with a 🔁 if recurring); the table view additionally shows the full range as "Period shown: start – end" on the table grid. (2026-07-21 update: a "Set Pay Period separately per department" checkbox used to sit alongside "Make this recurring," replacing the single shared Pay Date with one Start Date + Period + Make recurring block per department. Removed along with the Department filter — see the tried-and-rejected note below.)

Note — "paid," not "owed" (2026-07-16, per direct instruction). This widget reports payroll that has already been paid within the selected period — it's an after-the-fact check of what went out, not a forward-looking view of an outstanding obligation. That's an important correction to how this was framed: the "Payment due" callout above every view used to name the pay date as if it were something still owed, which is backwards — the pay date shown is always in the past or present, never a future amount due. Relabelled to "Paid: date" everywhere it appears. The current-vs-prior comparison isn't affected by this correction — it's still comparing two already-paid periods against each other, which is exactly the kind of after-the-fact check this widget is for.

Note — pay-type categories replace the paycheck-stub breakdown (2026-07-16, per direct instruction). This widget's breakdown used to show Net Pay/Fed Tax/Benefits/State Tax/Retirement/Overtime — a gross-to-net breakdown of one paycheck's line items, more like reading a pay stub top to bottom. That's not the right lens here. It's now Regular, Vacation, OverTime, Sick, Double Time, Personal, Holiday, Misc, Other — the pay-type/earnings codes hours are actually coded under on a pay run, which is what "Distribution" should mean for this widget. This should be linkable in the real system — pay groups already tie to compensation records — but the exact field or table isn't confirmed; the original Purpose doc's formula (`SUM(PRHistoryCompensation.Amount) GROUP BY CompensationDistributionID, Name`) groups by compensation distribution, not by pay type, so there's likely a different dimension (an earnings/pay-type code) somewhere off `PRHistoryCompensation` or a related detail table that this widget would need instead. Flagged for the developer to dig into rather than assumed — see the Developer Punch List.

Compared to the current real system (Purpose doc): today's widget is a single fixed layout — a table and a pie chart shown side by side, always grouped by compensation category, with plain Beginning/Ending date pickers (defaulting 1 Jan–today), no comparison to any other period, no per-department scheduling of any kind, no recurring option, no drill-down, and no department filter. This redesign changed some of that and, as of 2026-07-21, has come back around on one part of it: Bar is still the new default (pie/donut alone doesn't hold up once an org has more than ~5 categories), Pie and Table are still kept as full peers rather than dropped, the raw date pickers are still named, Pay-Date-anchored periods with an explicit recurring flag, and a current-vs-prior comparison is still shown everywhere. But the Department filter and department-level rollup this redesign had added on top of the legacy design — see the tried-and-rejected note below — were cut back out on review, landing this widget back on the legacy design's own "no department filter" position, just with the other improvements above kept. A drill-through to the Payroll History module remains specced as a genuinely new feature the current system has no equivalent of.

Tried and rejected — Department filter, per-department rollup, and "Separate By Department" (2026-07-21, design call with Jo). This redesign added a Department filter (All Departments · Finance · Admin · Ministry · Facilities) on top of the legacy design, which never had one. With it: Bar/Pie/Table showed one row per department at "All Departments," each department's bar stacked by its own Distribution composition; drilling into one department showed that department's own Distribution breakdown instead; and a "Set Pay Period separately per department" checkbox let each department run on its own Start Date/Period/Recurring rather than one shared Pay Date. Rejected on review. Per direct instruction, this was "kind of already a bit of a miss match" — the Department field was never confirmed to exist on the real `PRHistory`/`PRHistoryCompensation` tables in the first place (see the open item this closes, below), and it added a whole extra navigation layer on top of what this widget is actually named and built to show: a breakdown by Distribution. Cut entirely, not reworked — this widget goes back to always showing the Distribution breakdown directly, matching the legacy design's own scope, while keeping every other improvement from this redesign (Bar default, Pie/Table peers, Pay-Date anchoring, recurring flag, current-vs-prior comparison). Removed from `Dashboard Widget Mockups.html`: the Department filter entry in `MOCK_DATA.filters[3]`; the Finance/Admin/Ministry/Facilities buckets in `MOCK_DATA.series[3]` (only 'All Departments' remains, as the sole bucket); the department-rollup branch, `catBreakdown`, and `hbarStacked()` stacked-bar rendering in `WRENDER[3]`; the `deptName` parameter on `w3PeriodRange()`; and the "Set Pay Period separately per department" checkbox and its per-department Start Date/Period/Recurring fields in `_renderFltBody()`. Kept here as history per the project's rule against deleting rejected ideas outright.

Also raised, and also dropped for now — a deeper Distribution breakdown (2026-07-21, design call with Jo). Per direct instruction: "the break down of Distributions would be amazing improvement but concept of how it should work is not clear currently." The idea — drilling into a single Distribution (e.g. "Regular") to see some further level of detail beneath it — isn't built anywhere in this mock and wasn't started as part of this pass; there's no clear concept yet of what that further detail would even be (per-employee amounts? per-pay-run history? something else?), so nothing here was designed or coded toward it. Per direct instruction, this is worth raising as an open question to the developer in Step 5's API topic in a later pass — specifically, whether the backend can identify a real data link that would support drilling from a Distribution into further detail. If it can't, the idea is fully dropped rather than half-built on a guess. Scope note: that Step 5 conversation is explicitly a separate, later pass — not part of this mock_work-only review — so nothing has been changed in `Step 5 - API documents` yet.

Open items — not built, flagged rather than guessed at: (1) Department field is not confirmed to exist on the real `PRHistory`/`PRHistoryCompensation` tables — backend needs to confirm before this filter can go live. Closed 2026-07-21, superseded by rejection: moot — the Department filter itself was cut on review with Jo, not because backend confirmed or denied the field. See the tried-and-rejected note above. (2) Drill-through target page (the Payroll History module) isn't confirmed yet. (3) The Data Table Sort rule (fixed alphabetical, with a user toggle to Amount descending) — only the fixed alphabetical default is built; the toggle isn't. (4) Monthly's 30-day approximation vs. a true calendar-month subtraction, noted above. (5) "Make this recurring" is stored and displayed but is a flag only in this mockup — nothing here actually advances a period forward over calendar time; that's real scheduling logic for the backend, not something a static mock can demonstrate. (6) The new pay-type breakdown (Regular/Vacation/OverTime/Sick/Double Time/Personal/Holiday/Misc/Other) is mock data only — it should be linkable via pay groups, but the real field/table backing it isn't confirmed; needs developer investigation before build. (7) New 2026-07-21: whether a deeper breakdown within a single Distribution is buildable at all — see "Also raised, and also dropped for now" above; needs a dev question in Step 5's API topic in a later pass before this goes anywhere.

What carried over from her build, faithfully: her two views over the same aggregated runs (a sortable table and a donut, behind a Table/Chart toggle at Explore; at Detail both are shown side by side and the toggle disappears since both fit); her scope system (All distributions, By pay type, or one specific distribution, chosen from a scope chip whose popover lists every distribution with its fixed color dot; drilling into one distribution happens IN PLACE via that chip, with a context line under the total naming the drill, not via a modal); her three table shapes per scope, including the four-column pay-type table with distribution color badges and sr-only per-row text; her sort headers (amount descending by default, text columns ascending on first click, every click flips the active column); her donut (blue ramp arcs, center total, legend with money and percent, hover sync that dims the other segments and highlights the matching legend row); her percent-of-total bars as role=img with the real figure always beside them as text; her period chip and popover with the Custom time span row FIRST, inline From/To date fields that always show the dates currently in effect, a fixed 340px popover width so typing never jitters, and the focus-restore bookkeeping so re-renders never drop the caret out of a date field (SME: a custom range is always available); her empty state ("No payroll runs in this range", inbox icon, no call to action) which keeps the period and scope chips visible so the customer can always navigate back out; and her instant client-side recompute behaviour: every period, scope, sort and view change re-aggregates the runs in memory with no fetch and no skeleton, exactly as her demo behaves. Her one piece of dead code (an unreachable duplicate pr-range-set branch referencing a function that does not exist) was deliberately NOT ported. THE ONE DESIGN CHANGE, per direct instruction: the period presets are now exactly This month / This period / This quarter, in that order (smallest first), with This month the default (owner decision), replacing her This month / This quarter / All time / This year set. Window definitions follow the Time Window Module: This month is the current calendar month; This period is the current fiscal period, which in this mock resolves to the same July window because the mock's fiscal calendar equals calendar months (the API keeps window=month and window=period distinct); This quarter is ROLLING, the last 3 months back from the as-of date, not the calendar quarter. No grain toggle and no bucketed time axis were added (this widget aggregates a window into one breakdown, it is not a time series), and there is deliberately NO prior-period comparison anywhere: Jo's sign-off finding F3 rejected comparison features for this widget and that decision is respected here, which also supersedes the earlier A-option's always-visible change badges under F. Jo's 12 biweekly runs were extended by ONE deterministic 13th run (Jul 29 2026, same seeded generator) and the mock as-of anchor set to Jul 31 2026 per the project's end-of-July convention, so the three presets show meaningfully different totals: This month holds 3 runs (Jul 1, Jul 15, Jul 29), This quarter holds 7 (May 6 through Jul 29). Exports are honest stubs in the card's 3-dot menu (CSV/Excel/PDF, F-only items, toast feedback, no fake download), matching her registry's export actions. Sizing follows Jo's three-tier model via the same fc-fmode mechanism as W01/W02 (no Small under Final; Glance, Explore and Detail wording and her tier proportions), and the KPI card title reflects the widget's own scope ("Payroll Distributions: [scope]") through the existing FC_KPI_HEADLINE plumbing. Presets extended same day per direct instruction: This year (ROLLING, the last 12 months back from the as-of date per the Time Window Module, Aug 1 2025 through Jul 31 2026 here, not the calendar year Jo's original used) and All time (every run in the data, no lower bound) were restored from Jo's original set, appended after This quarter to keep the smallest-first order, with This month still the default and the Custom time span row still first; with only about six months of mock history the two new presets currently return the same 13 runs, which is expected.

Purpose
Answers one question at a glance: are we keeping pace with the year on every remittance pledge? The headline is the total paid so far, badged On track or Behind pace against the share of the calendar year elapsed, with a "% of pledged" goal pill, so the pacing read is never left for the reader to work out by eye. Each activity reads two ways over the same figures: a full report table (Activity, Annual, YTD Expected, YTD Paid, Outstanding, % Paid, with a Total row) and a pacing-bars view (one bar per activity with an "expected by now" marker), behind a Table / Pacing Bars toggle at Explore; at Detail both are shown side by side and the toggle disappears. "Expected by now" is the annual pledge times the share of the calendar year elapsed (the verified production basis for apportionments), and pacing is measured cumulatively to the end of the chosen receipts window (only receipts on or before that end date count), so changing the window genuinely re-computes the figures. Every row drills to its payment history, with a plain year-end catch-up line on any activity that is behind. Ported from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo remittance design as this widget's Final, recomposed with the locked Version A report table as the default view and a 4-step pacing colour scale.
Customer Research — What We're Working Off
business_center
Virtuous — Pledge Tracking open_in_new
No dedicated competitor product for denominational apportionment/remittance tracking exists — this is a niche church-finance concept — so the benchmark is the general nonprofit "Pledge vs. Received" pattern instead of one named direct competitor. That pattern has an established fulfillment-rate formula (Received ÷ Pledged × 100, healthy range 85–95%, per DonorSearch), which is the direct reason overall % Paid is the KPI headline. Virtuous's pledge-tracking approach is the closest reference for the progress-bar default.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

One filled bar per activity type — the filled portion is what's been received, the empty remainder is outstanding, so the gap itself is visible at a glance without reading numbers. Progress Bars is the default because it's the single most common visualisation for this exact "pledge vs received" metric across every source reviewed.

Small shows 2-3 activity types with no Switch View — a glance-sized read. Medium and Large show the active view (bars or table) across 4-5 or all activity types respectively, with full values and %. The KPI headline is overall % Paid — received divided by pledged across every activity type — the named industry fulfilment-rate metric, not an internally invented number, and it carries no filter at all since the Fiscal Year filter was removed and nothing else applies at that size.

Three fixes made as part of this check: (1) the KPI-size card wasn't implemented — added, using the "overall % Paid" headline the doc specifies. (2) Small was showing one big "Overall received X%" headline plus a single activity's bar, instead of 2-3 bars — one of the two KPI concepts the doc's "What Got Cut" section says was dropped; fixed to show the same progress-bar list every other size uses, and also now forces the default (non-table, non-pie) view at Small the way the doc's "no Switch View" note implies. (3) the Date Range filter's third value didn't match the doc ("Year to Date" vs. the doc's "Custom") and a dead "Year" filter was still present despite the doc saying it was removed — both corrected. Not fixed, flagged instead: Custom Date Range should reveal Beginning/Ending fields per the doc, same open item as W03's Pay Period; and the doc calls this filter "Activity Type" while the render, mock data and citations all consistently call it "Campaign" — worth reconciling one way or the other rather than left mismatched.

Final build (2026-07-27). Built as the Final from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo remittance widget (her rem block), per direct instruction, as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[4]; the A/B/C branches stay untouched and reachable from the design-option switch at the top of this section, with Final as the default. What carried over from her build, faithfully: her pacing header (total paid, an On track / Behind pace badge that reads the point gap and dollar shortfall against the share of the calendar year elapsed, and a "% of pledged" goal pill); her Receipts through date chip as the ONLY filter and the ONLY fetch (presets Today and End of last month plus a date field committed by Refresh, read from the DOM at commit time; a change shows an 800ms chip spinner and skeleton, while sort, view and drill are instant client re-renders); her leap-aware pacing maths (expected by now = annual times day-of-year / days-in-year, the verified production basis, never a fake 100%); her sortable table and per-activity pacing bars with the "expected by now" marker and formatted hover card; her payment-history drill (a modal listing the receipts on or before the date, with a plain year-end catch-up line on a behind activity, unpaid amounts carrying forward); her purposeful empty state (volunteer_activism icon); and her accessibility layer (sr-only values per row and bar, role=img bars, aria-haspopup chip, role=dialog modal, setStatus announcements, prefers-reduced-motion). THE COMPOSITION, per the owner's decisions: the DEFAULT view is the locked Version A report table (Activity with a paid-of-annual sub and a mini pacing bar, then Annual, YTD Expected, YTD Paid, Outstanding, % Paid, with a Total row that cross-foots and the caption "Expected-to-date reflects N% of the year elapsed", N computed from the Receipts through date), rendered in Jo's visual language; the alternate view is Version B's pacing-bars presentation built with Jo's pbar component (one full-width bar per activity, a "$paid, $expected by now" caption and a colour legend), reached by a 2-way Table / Pacing Bars toggle in the header at Explore. Glance is Jo's compact pacing card; Detail shows the table and the pacing bars as two synced panels over the same date and sort, with the toggle hidden. THE ONE KNOWING DEVIATION from Jo (owner decision): a 4-step pacing colour scale on the bar fill, the % Paid table cell and the status chips, keyed to gap = %paid minus %year in percentage points: Ahead (>= +5) strong green, On pace (-5 to +5) soft green, Behind pace (-15 to -5) amber, Far behind pace (below -15) red; fully-paid is Ahead, no-pledge is neutral grey. The .pbar-gap expected strip and the amethyst marker stay amethyst, since they encode expectation, not status. Colour is never the only signal: a text status chip (Ahead / On pace / Behind pace / Far behind pace / Paid in full / No pledge) plus values-as-text accompany every bar, and the scale is defined once as a remF function with matching CSS classes. FILTER MODEL: the Receipts through date replaces the old Date Range / Activity Type dropdowns entirely (no month presets), which for THIS build resolves the two Step 4 blocking rows (the Custom date-field reveal and the Activity Type / Campaign naming mismatch) and the recorded W04 KPI-filter conflict, since there is now a single, real, working date control and no stub dropdown; those rows stay open in the Step 4 doc for the old design pending the separate docs pass. Data note: the F branch's activities live in standalone REMF_ constants next to WRENDER[4] (deliberately not MOCK_DATA entries, so mock-data.master.js needs no re-sync; the A/B/C mock series are untouched), engineered so that at the mock anchor of 2026-07-31 (about 58% of the year elapsed) there is at least one activity in each of the four colour bands plus one no-pledge neutral row. Sizing follows Jo's three-tier model via the same generic fc-fmode mechanism as W01/W02/W03 (no Small under Final; Glance, Explore and Detail wording and her tier proportions), and the KPI card title reflects the widget's own pacing scope through the existing FC_KPI_HEADLINE plumbing.

Pacing refinement (2026-07-28). Two changes, both leaving the composition, the toggle, the synced Detail, the receipts-through fetch and the drill exactly as above. First, the pacing-bars presentation now uses Option B's bar STRUCTURE rather than Jo's pbar strip-and-marker: each bar is a fill whose width is paid over the total pledge, with a thin navy vertical TICK overhanging the track at the expected position (title "Expected by now: $X"), a caption "$paid paid · $expected expected by now" (middot separator, no em dash), and a legend row explaining the fill bands and the expected tick. The 4-step colour scale is KEPT and still lives on the FILL (Ahead / On pace / Behind pace / Far behind pace, plus Paid in full and No pledge); the tick is deliberately navy because it encodes the expected position, not the status. The same fill-plus-tick structure now drives the Table mini bar in the Activity column and the Glance mini bar, so all three read identically; the old amethyst .pbar-gap strip and .pbar-mark marker (and their legend swatches) were removed. Second, and more substantive, the pacing MATH changed from the calendar-year approximation to per-pledge TERM, per dev confirmation: every pledge now carries its own BeginDate and EndDate (plus Frequency and Duration, mirroring dbo.RM_Pledge) and a total-pledge amount over that term, and "expected by now" is total times the share of THAT pledge's own term elapsed (termDays = end - begin, elapsedDays = clamp(receiptsThrough - begin, 0, termDays), pace = elapsed / term), with the gap and the 4 colour thresholds measured against each pledge's own pace rather than the day-of-year fraction. The table columns were relabelled Annual/YTD to Pledge/Expected/Paid accordingly, the "N% of the year elapsed" caption became "each pledge's own term (start to end date)", and the header badge, the drill note (which now references the pledge's end date, not year-end) and every tooltip were reworded off the calendar-year basis. To prove the term math, the mock now includes a MULTI-YEAR pledge (Capital Campaign, a 3-year term Jul 2025 to Jun 2028): at the 2026-07-31 anchor it paces on-time against its own term (about 36% elapsed, 33% paid) but would read far behind against calendar-2026 (58% of the year) - exactly the case term pacing exists to get right. The data is still engineered so all four colour bands plus a neutral no-pledge row are present at the anchor, and overall the pledges are behind pace (paid 36,500 against 40,385 expected, about a 3,885 shortfall). No em dashes anywhere in the build.

Colour scale + Option B bar restyle (2026-07-28). Two owner-driven changes on top of the term-pacing build; the composition, toggle, synced Detail, receipts-through fetch and drill are unchanged. First, the pacing bar now renders exactly like Option B's Dashboard bar rather than a reskinned pbar: a single flat full-width rounded light-grey track (about 9px, 6px for the Table and Glance mini bars), one flat fill from the left whose width is paid over the total pledge in the solid band colour, and a thin (2px) dark navy vertical tick at the expected position (title "Expected by now: $X"), with the label and % paid on the row above and a "$paid paid · $expected expected by now" caption below (middot, no em dash). The same flat fill plus dark tick now drive the Table Activity-column mini bar and the Glance bar, so all three read identically, and the legend below the Pacing bars view shows the four band swatches plus the dark expected tick (hidden at Glance). Any leftover Jo pbar gap-strip and marker styling is gone from the remF build. Second, and the substantive change: the colour scale is no longer the percentage-point gap; it is now DAYS AHEAD OR BEHIND SCHEDULE, computed per pledge from its own term. For each pledge we take paidEquivalentDays = (paid / total) times termDays (the point in the term the paid amount corresponds to) and daysAhead = paidEquivalentDays minus elapsedDays. The bands, defined once as remFBandFromDays with matching CSS classes, are: 30 or more days ahead dark green (remf-ahead, chip "30+ days ahead"); within 30 days either side on track green (remf-onpace, chip "On track"); 30 to 60 days behind amber (remf-behind, chip "About a month behind"); more than 60 days behind red (remf-farbehind, chip "60+ days behind"); fully paid maps to the dark green with chip "Paid in full"; no pledge is neutral grey with chip "No pledge". The class names are unchanged so nothing else breaks; only the selection logic and the fill colours changed (remf-ahead #1b7a3d, remf-onpace #2e9e4f, remf-behind fill #e0952b, remf-farbehind fill #c0392b). The same day-based band colours the bar fill, the % Paid table cell and the status chip, and colour is never the only signal: the plain-language chip and the values sit beside every bar, and the exact day count is surfaced in the hover card ("About 47 days behind schedule") and the drill note. The header pace badge and shortfall keep their formula (aggregate expected versus paid sums) and wording. The mock data was re-tuned so that at the 2026-07-31 anchor every day-band is present: Outreach is 30+ days ahead (dark green), the multi-year Capital Campaign is on track against its own three-year term (green) yet would read far behind against calendar-2026, Clergy Pension is about a month behind (amber), General Fund is 60+ days behind (red), District Mission Share is paid in full, and Youth Ministry is the no-pledge neutral row; overall the portfolio is behind pace (paid 36,400 against 40,385 expected, about a 3,985 shortfall). FC_VERSION[4] stays 2.0. No em dashes anywhere in the build.

Pledge-drill refinement (2026-08-08, v2.1, per direct instruction). Four owner changes, all additive to the working Final and scoped to the remF branch only. (1) YTD Paid column. The activity table's paid-to-date column is relabelled "YTD Paid" and kept in its legacy position (Pledge, then Expected, then YTD Paid, then Outstanding, then % Paid); only YTD Paid was added, not a separate YTD Expected, and the existing paid-to-date figure was reused rather than duplicated. (2) The activity-click popup is removed from the table but kept rollback-able. Clicking an activity no longer opens the payment-history modal; the modal code (remFDetailModalHTML / remFRenderModal) is untouched and gated behind a new constant REMF_USE_POPUP, which defaults to false. Setting REMF_USE_POPUP to true restores the old popup on activity click exactly as before. (3) Activity click expands an inline pledge table. With the popup off, clicking an activity row (in either the Table or Pacing bars view) toggles open an inline dropdown table of THAT activity's pledges, collapsed by default and expand/collapse per activity. Columns: Church/donor name, Begin date, End date, Goal (pledged), Paid, Outstanding, and a paired-text pacing status (never colour alone). Each pledge is paced on its OWN begin-to-end term: expectedByNow = goal times clamp(receipts-through date minus begin, 0, termDays) divided by termDays, and shortfall = expectedByNow minus paid. The default sort is shortfall DESCENDING (most behind pace at the top), so later pages are progressively healthier. Pagination is real, 20 per page (REMF_PAGE_SIZE), with a numbered pager; each activity seeds about 60 to 72 pledges (three or more pages) so paging is demonstrable. (4) Activity Paid and Outstanding stay aggregates. Each activity's pledge set is generated deterministically (a seeded PRNG, memoised on the activity) so that the pledge goals sum exactly to the activity's Pledge total and the pledge paids sum exactly to the activity's YTD Paid at the mock anchor, so activity Paid equals the sum of its pledges' Paid and activity Outstanding equals the sum of its pledges' Outstanding. Church/donor names come from a shared pool and may repeat across activities, but each activity's pledge set is its own unique data. The Table / Pacing bars toggle, the receipts-through chip, the Glance/Explore/Detail sizes, the states and the values-as-text accessibility all keep working. FC_VERSION[4] = 2.1. No em dashes in any new user-facing string.

Name column and Pacing Bars drill removal (2026-08-08, v2.2, per direct instruction). Two owner changes, both additive to the working Final and scoped to the remF branch only. The names are PERSON names in "Last, First" form (each remittance church is a CorePerson record), so the seeded pool (REMF_CHURCHES) now holds realistic person-style names such as "Whitfield, Dana" and "Bell, Marcus". Names may repeat across activities while each activity's pledge SET stays its own unique seeded data; the other columns (Begin, End, Goal, Paid, Outstanding, status) are unchanged. The bars, status chips and receipts-through chip on the Pacing Bars view are unchanged. FC_VERSION[4] = 2.2. No em dashes in any new user-facing string.

Pacing Bars popup: top 5 most behind (2026-08-08, v2.3, per direct instruction). One owner change, additive to the working Final and scoped to the remF branch only. The Pacing Bars view activity rows are clickable again: clicking a row (or pressing Enter/Space, aria-haspopup dialog) opens a popup built on the shell's existing modal pattern (remFBehindModalHTML, mounted by remFRenderModal). The popup's LOWER SECTION is no longer the receipts / last payments to the activity. It is now the activity's TOP 5 pledges most behind pace: that activity's pledges sorted by shortfall (shortfall = expectedByNow minus paid, using each pledge's own start-to-end term) descending, filtered to those actually behind (shortfall greater than 0), capped at 5, with no pager. Each row shows Name (CorePerson Last,First), Begin date, End date, Goal, Paid, Outstanding and a paired-text pacing status, reusing the same pledge-row markup as the Table drill. The section carries a "Most behind pledges" heading and a note: if 5 or more are behind it reads "Showing the 5 furthest behind of N pledges behind pace"; if fewer than 5 are behind it reads "Showing all N pledge(s) behind pace" (and shows only those); if none are behind it shows a clean "No pledges are behind pace" message. The receipts / payment-history content is REMOVED from this popup but the old code is preserved and rollback-able: remFDetailModalHTML is untouched and is rendered only when the modal is opened with mode 'history', which happens only on the Table-view activity click while REMF_USE_POPUP is true (still default false). The Table view inline paginated pledge drill, the Table / Pacing bars toggle, the receipts-through chip, YTD Paid column, the Glance/Explore/Detail sizes, the states and the values-as-text accessibility all keep working unchanged. FC_VERSION[4] = 2.3. No em dashes in any new user-facing string.

Receipts window: single cutoff to date range (2026-08-08, v2.4, per direct instruction). One owner change, additive to the working Final and scoped to the remF branch only. The single "Receipts through [date]" filter is replaced by a DATE RANGE, wired per the owner's behaviour (a): the range END is the pacing cutoff (all pacing stays cumulative to it) and the START frames the window (and is reserved for scoping a receipts list, of which there is none in this build, so START currently only drives the chip). (1) The filter popover now offers exactly THREE options and no Refresh button: This year (the default: start = 1 January of the end's calendar year, end = today, i.e. the calendar year to date, never called fiscal), Last 30 days (start = end minus 30 days, end = today), and Custom, which reveals inline From and To date fields (same reveal pattern as W01/W03's Custom row) and applies on the fields changing. The old Today / End of last month presets and the single "choose a date" input plus Refresh button are gone. (2) Selecting a preset applies immediately (both This year and Last 30 days end today); Custom applies when a From/To field changes, read from the DOM at change time, with the popover kept open and the caret restored via the existing REMF_FOCUS_ID bookkeeping so typing never drops focus. (3) The filter chip now reads "Receipts from [start] to [end]" with both dates formatted concisely (a shared year is shown once, e.g. "Receipts from Jan 1 to Jul 31, 2026"), replacing the old "Receipts through [date]" text. (4) Wiring: REMF_STATE gains range / rStart / rEnd; remFRangeBounds derives {start,end} for the active option and remFThru now returns that END, so every pacing formula (Expected paced to end, Paid = receipts with check date on or before end, Outstanding, % Paid, the per-pledge shortfall used by the Table drill and the Pacing Bars top-5-behind popup) is UNCHANGED, just driven by end. remFRangeStart / remFRangePhrase are new. Because This year and Last 30 days both end today, their headline pacing numbers are identical by design (owner's decision), differing only in the displayed window. The Table view inline paginated pledge drill, the Pacing Bars top-5 popup, the YTD Paid column, the Table / Pacing bars toggle, the Glance/Explore/Detail sizes, the states, the person Last,First names and the REMF_USE_POPUP rollback flag all keep working unchanged. FC_VERSION[4] = 2.4. No em dashes in any new user-facing string.

Purpose
Shows how much money is currently owed to the organisation in unpaid invoices and how long those invoices have been outstanding, so staff can prioritise which outstanding amounts need attention first.
Customer Research — What We're Working Off
business_center
GlobalData365 — Accounts Receivable Dashboard open_in_new
AR aging dashboards commonly combine a bar or donut chart with a sortable detail table — a pie chart as the sole view is explicitly called out as the wrong choice for aging data, which directly confirms the old design's pie chart was a real defect, already removed here. KPI snapshot tiles above the aging breakdown is a separately recommended combination (Vertaccount) — the basis for the doc's KPI+Bars default, discussed in Logic below.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Each bar is one age band (0-30 days through 90+), sized by amount outstanding, so older/riskier buckets are as easy to compare as recent ones — bars, not a pie, because aging data is sequential and a pie doesn't respect that order (the specific defect this redesign fixes). A Data Table alternate gives exact invoice counts and amounts per band.

Flag — the doc's actual default view isn't fully built. The locked doc's View 1 is "KPI Tiles + Aging Bars": four tiles (Total Outstanding, Overdue, Current, Oldest Invoice) above a 5-bucket bar chart. What exists in the render is three separate options that each cover part of that: Option A is the aging bars alone, Option C ("KPI Cards + Table") has a 2-tile KPI strip (Total Outstanding, Overdue 30+) but pairs it with a table, not bars, and has no "Current" or "Oldest Invoice" tile — that last figure also doesn't exist anywhere in the current mock data. This page shows Option A since the bar chart is the more heavily-emphasised finding in the research (the pie-was-wrong point), but it is not the full default view the doc describes. Combining the two properly, and deciding what "Oldest Invoice" should even mean here, needs your input rather than a guess.

Separately: the age bands themselves don't match either — the doc specifies 5 (0-30/31-60/61-90/91-120/121+, with 121+ always red and 91-120 amber); the render only has 4 (0-30/31-60/61-90/90+). Splitting that last bucket touches the mock data and the colour rule together, so it's flagged rather than changed tonight.

Two fixes made, both safe/cosmetic since neither field is read anywhere in the render: the "Account" filter (Main/Secondary Account — not a real thing in the doc) was replaced with the doc's actual Revenue Center and Source filters; and a dead "Year" filter was removed, matching the doc's "no Fiscal Year filter" note. The KPI-size card also wasn't implemented — added, using the doc's exact "Total Outstanding ($)" headline, which is at least unambiguous regardless of how the S/M/L question above gets resolved.

Her real sample numbers carry over verbatim in standalone ARF_ constants next to WRENDER[5] (not MOCK_DATA, so mock-data.master.js needs no re-sync; the A/B/C mock series are untouched): eight invoices totalling $33,530, with the oldest 121+ days bucket holding Cornerstone Academy INV-2903 (due Feb 28 2026, 145 days, $9,650) and Legacy Insurance Group / Legacy HR Dept INV-2890 (due Mar 1 2026, 144 days, $6,300) for a bucket total of $15,950. That inline note is a developer-facing signal that the selected invoices are intended to move to unposted transactions to begin processing; it is deliberately not wired to any backend, is not a toast or a new page, and is not final copy. Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Cost is derived as cost = enrolled x per-enrollee monthly Rate, which mirrors the real derivation confirmed in the codebase trace where a plan's cost is the SUM of IBEmployeePlan.Rate across its enrollees; the mock per-enrollee rates (Medical Base 450, Medical Buy Up 620, Delta Dental 38, Vision 9, Building 0) are illustrative (Rule 11) while the derivation is grounded. Purpose
Deposits on Hand shows the money your organization holds on behalf of others, such as congregation or member deposits that may earn interest. Staff see the total held, how it splits across account types and individual accounts, and how each balance is trending, with a scrubbable sparkline at Glance and a drill into any one account or type.
Customer Research — What We're Working Off
business_center
Xero Dashboard open_in_new
Bank/deposit-account balance widgets are typically simple — name and balance, grouped by type, shown in real time. No source reviewed treats reconciliation status as a standard feature of this specific widget type (the old A/B/C option concepts below, which were built around it, stay closed). Separately, period-over-period cash trend tracking is a standard treasury/liquidity dashboard pattern — this is why the rebuild below adds a real Trend view and comparison, on top of a colleague's own Table/Distribution/Trend design that the user asked to adopt directly.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Final build (2026-07-30). Built as the Final from Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo Deposits on Hand widget (her deposits block), per direct instruction, as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[7] (prefix depF); the A/B/C branches below stay untouched and reachable from the design-option switch at the top of this section, with Final as the default. It is a 1-to-1 copy of her design: her Glance card (scope chip, total balance, Compare To control, and a scrubbable sparkline of the total over the chosen window), her Table / Distribution / Trend view toggle, her account-type and account scope filter chip (a searchable popover listing All Accounts, account types, and individual accounts; scope and Compare To are instant client re-renders, matching her build which has no fetch for deposits), her Compare To options (previous week, month, quarter, fiscal year, calendar year) driving every percent change, her sortable Name / Type / Trend / Balance table with the account number under each name and a total row, her amethyst single-hue donut (top slices plus an Others bucket, a by-type or by-account breakdown toggle when All types), her multi-line Balance Trend with Total / By Account Type / By Account breakdown, line isolate, crosshair and hover tooltip, her side-by-side Balances plus Distribution layout at Detail, her account and type drill modal (opened from a table row, a donut slice, or a trend legend row, rendering the scoped widget with a Trend / Table toggle), and her empty ("No deposit accounts") and loading states. Her real sample numbers carry over verbatim in standalone DEPF_ constants next to WRENDER[7] (not MOCK_DATA, so mock-data.master.js needs no re-sync; the A/B/C mock series are untouched). Four-to-three tier mapping: Jo's deposits widget uniquely has FOUR tiers (kpi, wide, large, xwide); they are mapped to this project's three-size model as Glance = her kpi, Explore = her wide, Detail = her xwide, and her middle large tier is dropped (never rendered) to fit the three sizes. Sizing follows the same generic fc-fmode mechanism as W01-W06 (no Small under Final; Glance / Explore / Detail wording and her tier proportions), and the KPI card title reflects the widget's own scope through the existing FC_KPI_HEADLINE plumbing. Title: shown as "Deposits on Hand" for this build per management's rename, which Jo already uses; the project-wide rename from "Deposit Accounts" is a separate pending pass, so this is this build's own chrome and title only. FC_VERSION[7] = 2.0. No em dashes in any new user-facing string.

Owner-directed behaviour change (2026-07-30), a deliberate deviation from Jo's 1-to-1 copy. Three changes were made on top of the ported build, at the project owner's direction. First, the Table now paginates at 50 rows per page, with a pager (page N of M, prev/next, and a "showing X to Y of Z" count); sorting and filtering apply first, then the result is paginated, and the Total row plus the KPI headline still cross-foot over the full scoped set, not the visible page. To demonstrate this the mock account set was expanded past 50 (now 125 accounts total across the 12 types; the three named accounts are unchanged). Second, Distribution and Trend now use a single scope-dependent 2-option breakdown instead of the old 3-option one: at All Accounts the toggle offers Total and By Account Type (the standalone By Account option is removed so it never shows every individual account at once, and By Account Type is the default); at a selected account type it offers Total and By Account, showing the accounts within that type. Third, clicking a chart element no longer expands, focuses, or opens a drill modal on these two views: clicking an account TYPE series (a type slice in Distribution or a type line or legend row in Trend, at the All-Accounts level) sets the top-left scope filter to that type and switches the breakdown to By Account, so the chart re-renders showing that type's individual accounts; clicking an individual ACCOUNT series does nothing (it is the leaf); and resetting the top-left filter back to All Accounts returns to By Account Type. The same logic applies to both Distribution and Trend. The Table's own row click (opening the account modal), the Glance card, Compare To, sort, states, accessibility, colours, and Glance / Explore / Detail sizing are all unchanged. The old chart drill-modal helper (depFOpenType) is left defined but unused rather than deleted.

Owner-directed addition (2026-07-30). A "period" (fiscal period) option was added to the Compare To time-scale control, inserted between month and quarter, per direct instruction. It is a fiscal period in the Time Window Module sense (per-org fiscal calendar, spanning between a month and a quarter), distinct from a calendar month; its compare window and KPI delta compute to a value between the month and quarter cases.

The dated notes below (2026-07-09 through 2026-07-13) are the earlier Option A rebuild history, left untouched for the record; they describe the A/B/C options, not this Final.

Rebuilt 2026-07-09, per direct instruction to adopt a colleague's Table/Distribution/Trend design and add period-over-period comparison. Mock data is now 10 accounts across 5 real types (Checking, Savings, Certificate of Deposit, Restricted Funds, Grant Funds), each with a 12-month balance history, replacing the old 4-account reconciliation-status shape entirely.

Table (default view). Name, Inception Date, Account Number, Ending Balance, and a % Change column — always shown now (see Compare To below). Totals row at Large/Expanded. Account Type filter narrows this table only, matching the doc.

Distribution. A donut with the combined total in its centre. Reworked 2026-07-10, per direct instruction: grouping now follows the Account Type filter directly instead of always grouping By Type — "All Accounts" groups by type (fund-level: what's doing well or poorly), and picking one specific type drills into that type's own individual accounts (what's inside that fund).

Trend. Simplified 2026-07-12, per direct instruction: the "All accounts / 2 account types" in-card toggle wasn't working and is now removed entirely. Trend just plots whatever the Account Type filter (shown inline at the top) currently resolves to — "All Accounts" gives one aggregate line across every account, picking a specific type gives that type's own line only, in that type's fixed colour. Still one MONTH of data at daily granularity (~30 points) per the prior fix — X-axis = days of that month, Y-axis = dollar balance. Compare To overlays the SAME scope (all accounts, or the same type) from a comparable prior month — 1 or 12 months back — as a dashed line plotted day-aligned against the current month (Day 1 vs Day 1, Day 15 vs Day 15), not a single point delta. Daily figures are derived by interpolating between each month's own start/end balance (mock data has monthly, not daily, granularity) — the same simplification already used for W01's Weekly period view. The declining-account ▼▼▼ flag stays on the Table (next to the account name).

Compare To (Last Month/Last Year) drives every % change shown above — the Table's column, the KPI's delta, and the Trend's comparison lines. Simplified 2026-07-13, per direct instruction: "the compare function should only be from last month compared to this month and this time to this time last year" — "Last Quarter" and "None" are removed, and Last Month is now the default everywhere, so a comparison always shows (it's no longer optional). Lives in the 3-dot "Change filters" menu at every size, including KPI (trimmed to Compare To only, the same mechanism W01 uses for Fiscal Year) — deliberately not an inline dropdown anywhere on the card.

KPI and Small. Fixed 2026-07-13, per direct instruction ("it's supposed to be all the same component, just different filter applied... take from Large if there's a difference"): both used to stay pinned to an unfiltered "all accounts" total while Large correctly filtered by Account Type — that mismatch is what looked broken/inconsistent between sizes. Now every size reads the same filtered dataset and the same Compare To calculation. KPI shows the filtered total as a line-sparkline tile (matching the colleague's reference design) with a ▲/▼ delta badge, and its title now reflects the Account Type filter (e.g. "Total Balance — Checking"). Small now also shows the filter-tag chips (it skipped them before) and a % Change column next to Name/Balance, for the same 2-3 accounts Large would show first.

Large/Expanded. Repositioned 2026-07-11, per direct instruction: Account Type and Compare To now show as inline dropdowns at the very top of the card (reusing the same generic inline-filter row W01 already uses), on top of the 3-dot menu. The filter-tag chip row is dropped at this size — it was redundant once the dropdowns moved to the top, showing the same two filters twice.

Account Type filter data fixed (2026-07-13), per direct instruction ("only ever two type accounts are showing" flagged as a bug): every type previously had exactly 2 accounts — a perfectly uniform split that read as broken/fake rather than real filtering. Added Petty Cash Checking (Checking) and Grant Reserve 2024 (Grant Funds), so the filter now returns 3/2/2/2/3 accounts depending on type, not a flat 2 every time.

Fixed, real bug found while testing this rebuild (2026-07-10): the Trend chart rendered completely blank. It sized itself the same way W01's charts do (a `flex:1` fill), but that only works because W01's card body has a special CSS rule (`display:flex`) no other widget's card body has — so the chart's mount point was collapsing to zero height for W07. Switched to a fixed pixel height instead, which renders correctly regardless of that CSS rule.

Fixed, real bug found while testing this rebuild (2026-07-09): resizing a card's Widget size never correctly showed/hid the Switch chart type section for any widget except W01 — the trim logic only checked for a wrapper class that only W01's markup happens to have, and silently did nothing everywhere else. This is why "the 3-dot menu wasn't changing when changing size" — fixed generically (falls back to finding the section by its label text), so it now works for every widget, not just W07. Separately, the KPI and Small slots' own dropdowns here had no Switch chart type section at all, so resizing either bigger via its own menu could never reveal Distribution/Trend even once the content grew past Small/KPI — added the same section to both, correctly hidden by default and revealed once resized up.

Known limitation — the real Dashboard tab's Switch View menu still shows the old two-item "Account Cards / Table" list. That markup lives inside the gallery's single giant HTML line, which this session's tools can't safely read or edit (a direct read of it errors out at over 50,000 tokens for a handful of lines). Final Check above reflects the complete three-view rebuild; the live gallery's menu needs a manual pass to add Distribution and Trend as reachable options there too — flagged for follow-up, same treatment as W02's earlier Small-size dropdown gap.

Known limitation — the KPI/Small title's dynamic "— Account Type" suffix only shows on this Final Check page. It's wired through the same generic headline mechanism used for W01/W02 (`FC_KPI_HEADLINE`), which only exists on Final Check; the real Dashboard tab's KPI/Small titles for this widget live in that same unreadable/uneditable giant HTML line noted above, so their title text will keep reading a static "Total Balance" there even though the underlying figure is correctly filtered now. Same follow-up bucket as the Switch View menu gap.

Options B ("Balance Bars") and C ("Compact Table") are the old reconciliation-based concepts — left as-is, not rebuilt, since the doc already closed them ("cut entirely... remains closed") and they're not reachable from this Final Check page.

Ready to be reviewed by Jo
