W09 - Payroll Scheduled Time Off Final

Visual proof that this widget's final design matches what's actually rendered: the real widget card, chrome and all, shown at Glance, Explore and Detail using the same live renderer as the Dashboard tab, not a static mock. Built 2026-08-07, refined through 2026-08-08 (v2.7) from the owner-confirmed composition. Each calendar day of a request is its own line: a multi-day request (say the 12th to the 14th) is three separate day-lines, each individually shown, counted and approvable. Two views: an Approval Queue (default) grouped by Department (default) or Pay Group then Person then day-lines, where each person row carries an Info icon (a per-person popover of that person's time off this year by leave type as text, plus a coverage-overlap list of who else is off during the same dates with their department and pay group) and each pending day offers Approve, with a person bulk Approve all (N) that counts pending day-lines, an Undo that returns an approved day to Pending, and a three-way Show All / Pending / Approved status filter; and a Leave Calendar: a real month grid with prev / next month navigation, weekday headers, today marked, and per-day markers that are the person's initials coloured by approval status (green approved, yellow pending), with the day cell itself taking a priority colour (any pending yellow, else all approved green), so a mixed day reads its priority colour with differently-coloured initials inside. The status word is carried in each marker's title and label text and in the day-cell aria-label, so colour is never the only signal. A Department vs Pay Group grouping toggle drives the grouping and day-detail labels. Clicking any day (or a marker) opens a per-day detail popover of who is out, with each person's leave type and status listed as text. Statuses are Pending and Approved only, and leave-type icons have been removed everywhere (the type shows as a plain text label). Controls use Jo's segmented toggle pattern to match the other Finals. The earlier A/B/C options stay reachable from the design-option switch below.

Purpose
Gives supervisors a view of all scheduled time-off requests, grouped by department (or pay group) and shown per person as one line per day, with the ability to approve requests directly from the widget, plus a calendar view of who is out when for planning.
Customer Research - What We're Working Off
business_center
BambooHR - Time Off Management open_in_new
Leave-management dashboards should surface pending requests and a calendar view for planning, with one-click approve including bulk actions as the core manager interaction (Synergy Codes, Factorial). This is the direct basis for the two-view Final: an Approval Queue for the action and a Leave Calendar for planning. The Gusto / Rippling pending-first queue pattern informs the Show Pending default.
Logic - What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Final build (2026-08-07), composed per the owner-confirmed sheet. Built as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[9] (prefix payF); the A/B/C branches stay untouched and reachable from the design-option switch above, with Final as the default. Data lives in standalone PAYF_* constants next to WRENDER[9] (not MOCK_DATA, so mock-data.master.js needs no re-sync). Sizing follows Rule 12 (Glance / Explore / Detail, no Small) via the same generic fc-fmode mechanism as W01-W07. FC_VERSION[9] = 2.3 (2026-08-08 calendar refine, then marker initials). No em dashes in any user-facing string.

Refine pass (2026-08-07), per owner feedback. Three changes, all additive to the payF branch: (1) the Approval Queue top controls were restyled to Jo's segmented toggle pattern (her .vtoggle / .vt classes, scoped to .payf-root with the same Pathway tokens the other Finals use) so the view switch and the Show Pending / All / Approved filter read as clean as her widgets; (2) a Group by (Pay Group / Department) control was added to the Approval Queue, styled identically to the calendar's group-by, with the person shown under whichever subheading is active; (3) the Leave Calendar was rebuilt as a genuine month grid (weekday headers, real weeks x days cells, adjacent-month days greyed, today marked, prev / next month navigation with a clean empty-month state) using per-day leave-type icon markers, and the old table breakdown below the grid was removed.

Calendar refine (2026-08-08), per owner feedback, Leave Calendar view only. Two changes, both additive to the payF branch. (1) Colour by group, not by type. Day markers are now coloured by the active Group by dimension: each pay group (Group by = Pay Group) or each department (Group by = Department) gets its own stable palette colour from PAYF_PALETTE, assigned deterministically from the group's fixed index (payFGroupOrder / payFGroupColor) so a group is always the same colour across months. The leave type is now carried by the marker glyph and text label, freeing colour for the group. The legend became two parts, a group colour-swatch key for the active dimension plus a leave-type icon key, and flipping the Group by toggle recolours the markers and swaps the legend's group key. Colour is never the only signal (glyph shape + text labels remain). (2) Click a day or an icon to expand detail. A new day-detail dialog popover (payFDayDetail, Jo's bgt-pop card pattern scoped to .payf-root) opens on clicking a day cell or a marker, listing each person out that day with name, both Pay Group and Department, leave type (icon + label), hours, and status (Pending or "Approved by [name], [date]"); a marker click pre-focuses that person. It is informational (a footer hint points to the Approval Queue for approvals, no approve action here) and is keyboard reachable (day cells and markers are role=button and tabbable) and dismissible via the close control, click-away, or Escape. State lives in PAYF_STATE.dayDetail; view change and month nav clear it. FC_VERSION[9] bumped to 2.2.

View 1, Approval Queue (default). A clean row/column list with a Group by toggle: Pay Group (default) or Department as subheadings, each person shown by name directly under the active subheading, and under each person their entries: dates, leave type (a coloured type ICON plus text label), hours, and status. Status reads "Pending" or "Approved by [name], [date]". Approve controls: a person-level "Approve all (N)" bulk action and a per-entry Approve, with an Undo on approved entries. A Show Pending (default) / All / Approved status filter sits inline. This is the widget's core interaction and its reason for existing, so it leads. Composition note: this supersedes the Step 4 doc's Department then Employee then Day structure, per direct owner instruction 2026-08-07 (recorded as a version-tagged update; the old structure is preserved in the Step 4 Design History section).

View 2, Leave Calendar. A real month grid showing who is out when. Sunday-to-Saturday weekday column headers, a full weeks x days cell grid computed from the displayed month (adjacent-month days greyed, today outlined), and prev / next month navigation with a month + year label. Each out-day carries icon markers, one distinct material-symbols glyph per leave type (Vacation, Sick, Personal, Misc). Colour encodes the active Group by dimension (refine 2026-08-08): when Group by is Pay Group each pay group gets its own stable palette colour, when Department each department does, assigned deterministically from a fixed index so a given group is always the same colour across months. The leave TYPE is carried by the marker glyph shape plus its text label (in the tooltip, the legend and the day detail), so colour is never the only signal. A day with more people than fit shows a "+N" overflow. The Group by toggle (Pay Group default, or Department) drives the summary line, the marker colours, the legend contents and each marker's group label; flipping it recolours the grid and swaps the legend's group key. The legend has two parts: a colour swatch key for the active dimension's groups present that month, and a leave-type icon key, so both signals stay documented. Each marker also carries the person's initials next to its leave-type icon (refine 2026-08-08), derived from the name as first plus last initial (for example Dana Whitfield reads "DW"), with a single-name fallback to the first two letters; initials show at both Explore and Detail so there is a rough who-is-who at a glance, while the full name stays in the marker tooltip and the day detail. The "+N" overflow rule is unchanged. Detail size shows larger cells; Explore shows compact cells with the same icon-plus-initials markers. A month with no entries renders a clean empty-month state.

Day detail popover (refine 2026-08-08). Clicking a day cell, or a specific marker icon within it, opens an expanded detail for that day: a dialog popover (Jo's bgt-pop card pattern, scoped to .payf-root) listing each person out that day with their name, both their Pay Group and Department, the leave type (icon + label), hours, and status (Pending, or "Approved by [name], [date]"). Clicking a marker pre-focuses that person's row. It is informational only, with a footer hint that approvals are handled in the Approval Queue, so no approve action lives here. The popover is keyboard reachable (day cells and markers are role=button, tabbable, Enter / Space open) and dismissible three ways: the close control, click-away on the backdrop, or Escape. An empty day is not clickable and a month with no entries never opens it.

Approval Queue actions, Rejected status and four filters (2026-08-08, v2.4), per owner feedback. Three additive changes to the Approval Queue only (calendar untouched except the shared status model). (1) Three actions. Each person row now carries an Info icon that opens a per-person detail popover (reusing the day-detail popover card pattern): section (a) that person's time off this year totalled by leave type (Vacation, Sick, Personal, Misc, as day counts, excluding rejected), section (b) a list of other staff who have time off this year with each one's pay group and total days, for coverage context. It is informational only, keyboard reachable (the icon is role=button, tabbable) and dismissible via close control, click-away or Escape. Each pending entry now shows both an Approve and a Reject button; the person-level bulk actions are both present, Approve all (N) and a matching Reject all (N); Undo on a resolved entry returns it to Pending, reversing either. (2) Rejected is a real status alongside Pending and Approved: a rejected entry reads "Rejected by [name], [date]" (mirroring "Approved by [name], [date]") in a distinct red chip paired with a cancel icon and the text label, never colour alone (the Approved and Pending chips also carry an icon now). (3) The status filter became four chips, All / Pending / Approved / Rejected, Pending still the default; Approved shows only approved, Rejected only rejected, All everything. The F mock data was extended with some already-Rejected entries and earlier-month per-person history so the totals and coverage list have real data. All driver-verified 2026-08-08 (per-entry Approve+Reject and Info icon render; Reject sets Rejected and renders the rejected-by text; Undo reverses it; bulk Approve-all and Reject-all fire; the four filters each change output correctly; the Info popover opens with this-year totals by type and the other-staff list as DOM text and dismisses; status colour is always paired with text + icon). FC_VERSION[9] bumped to 2.4. No em dashes in any user-facing string. Backend-reality caveats (recorded in Widget_Specs, not shown on screen): Rejected is a NEW workflow state, the legacy/Modern PR_EmployeeOffSchedule model has only approve/unapprove via ApprovedDate with no rejected state, so a backend field and reject action are needed; and the Info panel's this-year totals by leave type and other-staff-off list are aggregations over PR_EmployeeOffSchedule (feasible, scoped to the supervisor's authorised groups) that are not existing endpoints.

Calendar colour language: group to status (2026-08-08, v2.5), per owner feedback, Leave Calendar view only. The calendar's colour now encodes approval STATUS, superseding the v2.2 "colour = group" scheme. (1) Colour by status. Approved = green (#2e7d32, aligned with the approved chip), Rejected = red (#c0392b, the reject red), Pending = amber (#c77d00, a legible take on the pending amber). (2) Day-cell priority. A day with multiple statuses takes one cell colour by priority: any entry Pending -> amber; else any Rejected -> red; else (all approved) -> green; days with no requests stay neutral. The cell shows a light tint plus an inset accent bar. (3) Per-marker status. Each person marker is coloured by that person's own entry status, so a mixed day visibly shows different-coloured markers inside the priority-coloured cell; each marker keeps its leave-type glyph, the person initials, a paired status glyph (check / schedule / cancel) and a title + sr-only label naming the status word, and the day cell aria-label names its overall status, so colour is never the only signal. (4) Status legend replaces the group colour-swatch key (green Approved, amber Pending, red Rejected, each swatch paired with its glyph and word); the leave-type icon key stays, and initials now carry who-is-who. (5) Group by still works for grouping in the queue and the day-detail (and each marker's group label), but no longer drives colour; flipping it changes grouping and labels, not the day colours. All driver-verified 2026-08-08: the priority rule (a pending+approved+rejected day renders amber; an approved+rejected day renders red; an all-approved day renders green; a no-request day is neutral), per-marker status colour, the status legend (not groups), status paired with a non-colour signal in the DOM, and that flipping Group by leaves the day colours unchanged, alongside all prior assertions. FC_VERSION[9] bumped to 2.5. No em dashes in any user-facing string.

Info panel lower section: same-dates overlap (2026-08-08, v2.6), per owner feedback, Approval Queue Info popover only. The per-person Info popover's LOWER section was reworked; the TOP section (that person's time off this year by leave type) is unchanged. The old lower list ("other staff off this year" with each one's total days) was the wrong signal and is superseded. It now shows a coverage-overlap list: who else is off during the SAME dates as this person, computed as every OTHER person whose time-off entry overlaps ANY of this person's own entries (two entries overlap when they share the same month and year and their day ranges intersect, startA ≤ endB and startB ≤ endA). Each overlapping entry is listed once with that person's name, department and pay group, the overlapping dates (with the leave-type icon) and the leave type plus its status. The list is status-agnostic so the supervisor sees the full picture. When no one overlaps, a clean "No one else is off during these dates." line shows. The subject person's own department and pay group now sit under their name in the panel header. The F mock data was extended (a Grace Lin August entry) so the overlap list is populated for at least one person while others (for example Priya Nandakumar) show the clean empty line. Driver-verified 2026-08-08: opening Info for a person whose dates overlap another shows that person WITH department AND pay group AND the overlapping dates as DOM text; the old per-other-person "days off this year" total is gone from the lower list; the subject's dept + pay group render in the header; a no-overlap person shows the clean line; the top per-person year totals still render; all prior assertions stay green. FC_VERSION[9] bumped to 2.6. No em dashes in any user-facing string. Backend-reality caveat (recorded in Widget_Specs, not shown on screen): this overlap/coverage list is an aggregation over PR_EmployeeOffSchedule (other employees with overlapping OffDate ranges, scoped to the supervisor's authorised groups), feasible but not an existing endpoint.

Owner changes (2026-08-08, v2.7), four applied together. These supersede parts of the notes above; the superseded descriptions (the v2.4 Rejected workflow, the leave-type icon markers, and the v2.5 three-colour Pending > Rejected > Approved priority) are kept above as the dated record. (1) Each day is its own line. A multi-day request is now expanded to one entry per calendar day in payFFlat (single-day d = dEnd, per-day hours, a unique per-day _id), so a request for the 12th to the 14th is three separate day-lines. The Approval Queue lists one line per day per person, the per-person "Approve all (N)" and every pending count count DAY-lines, the Leave Calendar marks each day, and the Info coverage-overlap compares at day level. (2) Rejected removed from both views: no Reject button, no bulk Reject all, no Rejected status or "Rejected by" text, no Rejected filter chip (filters are now All / Pending / Approved), no red status colour, and the Rejected mock entries were converted to Pending or Approved. Undo still returns an Approved day to Pending. The calendar day-colour priority is now any Pending -> yellow, else all-approved -> green. (3) Group by Department is first and the default in both views (Pay Group is the second option); PAYF_STATE.queueGroup and calGroup default to dept. (4) Leave-type icons removed everywhere: the type shows as a plain text label in the queue rows, the day detail and the Info panel, and the calendar legend's leave-type icon key is gone (a simple status colour key remains, green Approved / yellow Pending). A calendar marker is now the person's initials coloured by status, with no leave-type icon and no separate status glyph; the status word stays in the marker title, the sr-only label and the day-cell aria-label so colour is never the only signal. All driver-verified 2026-08-08: a 3-day request renders as 3 queue day-lines and 3 calendar day-markers; no Reject button / Reject all / Rejected chip / Rejected status / red colour anywhere; filter chips are exactly All / Pending / Approved; Group by defaults to Department and lists Department before Pay Group in both views; no leave-type icon glyph in queue rows or calendar markers (type is text); day colours are only green / yellow with priority Pending > Approved; approve + undo + bulk approve-all fire; Info overlap + this-year totals render as text; month nav + day detail work; no em dashes. FC_VERSION[9] bumped to 2.7. No em dashes in any user-facing string.

Outstanding state (2026-08-08, v2.8), per owner change, three placements. An entry (day-line) is Outstanding when its date is strictly BEFORE the current date (the established today anchor, Aug 7 2026) AND it is still Pending. A past date that is Approved is NOT outstanding; a Pending date that is today or in the future is normal Pending, NOT outstanding. Outstanding is a past-due pending day. (1) Calendar: an Outstanding marker is RED (#c0392b); the day-cell colour priority is now any Outstanding -> red, else any Pending -> yellow, else all approved -> green. Each marker is coloured by its own state; the marker title and sr-only label and the day-cell aria-label name the state word ("Outstanding" / "Pending" / "Approved"), so colour is never the only signal, and red = Outstanding was added to the status legend. (2) Glance (KPI): an Outstanding count shows as its own figure next to the Pending figure; crucially the Pending count EXCLUDES outstanding (Pending = pending dated today or later; Outstanding = pending dated before today), so the two are mutually exclusive and partition the pending set with no double count. The old "Out this week" secondary was dropped so the two priority figures read cleanly at 288x176. (3) Approval Queue (light touch): outstanding day-lines carry a red "Outstanding" tag and a red left accent; they are still Pending, so they still appear under the Pending filter and still count in the existing queue header and per-person pending counts for this pass (no new filter chip was added). All driver-verified 2026-08-08: the outstanding classifier is date-before-today AND pending (approved-past and pending-future are NOT outstanding); a past pending day renders red on the calendar with a red marker, a future pending day is yellow, an approved day is green; the legend includes red = Outstanding; Glance shows a Pending figure and a separate Outstanding figure with Pending excluding the outstanding ones (Pending + Outstanding partition the pending set); queue outstanding rows carry the red Outstanding tag; approving an outstanding day makes it green/approved and drops it from both Pending and Outstanding; month nav, day-detail, Info panel, per-day lines and the Department default all still work; no em dashes. FC_VERSION[9] bumped to 2.8. No em dashes in any user-facing string. Open question flagged to the owner: whether the queue's Pending filter and its header/person pending counts should also exclude outstanding (or gain an Outstanding chip), which this pass deliberately did not change.

Glance (KPI). Two figures side by side: a Pending count and a separate Outstanding count (v2.8). Pending excludes outstanding (pending dated today or later); Outstanding is past-due pending (pending dated before today). The two are mutually exclusive. The earlier "Pending Approvals headline plus Out this week secondary" is superseded (the Out this week secondary was dropped, owner change 2026-08-08).

Pay-group data is mock (Rule 11), and the backend link is indirect. The fixed five-slot pay-group model (A to E) plus Normal Payroll lives on PREmployeeCompensationDetail.PayGroup (smallint; labels from PRCompany.PayGroupName), linked to an employee only INDIRECTLY through their compensation detail. The time-off record PREmployeeOffSchedule has no pay-group field, so grouping the queue by pay group requires a backend join through compensation detail (precedent: pay-group filtering exists in PRTimeCardRepository). This is not a confirmed direct field. Carried backend gaps from Step 1: the inline approve/reject action endpoint, the approval-authority (who-can-approve) scoping, and org-configured custom leave-type labels are all not implemented in the Modern API. None of this is shown on-screen; it is recorded in the Widget_Specs write-up for whoever takes this to development.

GlobalData365 — Fixed Assets Dashboard open_in_new
Fixed-asset dashboards commonly use pie charts by class/category alongside a full lifecycle table, with filters by year/class/location. Pie/donut charts are only recommended for small category counts — since this widget's Group By options range from low-cardinality (Class) to high-cardinality (Room, Asset Account), keeping both a bar and a donut view as peers is the standard-supported answer, not a compromise.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

2026-08-30, the Final (option F), per direct instruction "copy Jo's 1 to 1". The Final is Jo's Fixed Asset Values widget ported into this file with a faF prefix, not a composition of options A, B and C. Its filters are hers and are the doc's three: Group By across 6 dimensions (Class, Building, Room, Asset Account, Accumulated Depreciation Account, Expense Account), Specific Group as a dependent field that repopulates when the dimension changes, and Financial Measure across exactly the 5 money figures (Capitalized Value, Cost, Depreciable Value, Accumulated Depreciation, Net Value). Its composition is driven by size (Rule 12), not by a chart-type switch: Glance is the measure total plus asset count, Explore is the per-asset table, Detail is that table with a donut beside it. There is no bar chart and no Switch View in her build, so the chart-type menu is hidden while F is active rather than offering views that do nothing.

Options A, B and C (superseded, kept for comparison). Each bar is one category, sized by net book value, which is the default view. Donut and Table alternates are available via Switch View. Small shows the top 3 categories in whichever view is active; Medium shows all categories; Large adds totals.

Resolved 2026-08-30 by the Final. Was flagged: the doc's real filter model isn't built. The locked doc calls for three filters working together: Group By (a dimension switcher across Class, Building, Room, Asset Account, Accumulated Depreciation Account and Expense Account, which changes what the data is grouped BY), Specific Group (a dependent field that narrows to one group within whichever dimension is selected), and Financial Measure (which of five money figures the chart and KPI focus on). All three are present in the Final. The flag still stands for options A, B and C, which have only a single flat "Asset Category" filter (Buildings, Vehicles, Equipment, IT Assets, Furniture) with no dimension switching, no dependent field and no measure selector. Purpose
An actionable approval-process board for purchase order requests. The default Kanban view puts one column per approval state (Pending, Approved, Rejected, the states on the real record screen's Approvals tab) with the oldest, longest-waiting requests at the top of each column and each card showing its item age. Dragging a card to another column actions the request: a popup asks for a Reason/note (mirroring the real Approvals tab), Confirm applies the move and records the note on the request, Cancel reverts. The Approval Path filter narrows to one customer-defined path (Administration, Education Ministry, Everyone, QA Path in this mock), populated from the orders matching the current status and disabled when only one path exists; the status filter hides irrelevant columns. Selecting a card or a table row opens the PO record (Detail, Approvals, Attachments, Note, Payment Approval tabs), the same screen as today; in this mock that is a modal, and recorded notes appear in its Note tab. Card colour carries the sub-state, always paired with text: an unpaid Approved card is neutral with a "Payment: not paid" badge, and clicking it opens the Payment Approval tab where entering the invoice numbers turns the card green ("Payment: paid"); a held card is yellow with a lock and its reason, and cannot be dragged until the hold (Put on hold / Remove hold in the record modal, each with a reason note, mirroring the real Approvals tab's Hold + Reason) is removed. The PO Table second view adds Department, Year and Overdue as Table-only filters, with overdue rows flagged in red plus a text flag. Glance shows three state-count cards, Pending first, with the pending-request count and outstanding total. Access rules carry over: admins see all orders, others only orders on their approval paths. Forward-design note: the legacy widget never shows rejected orders and has no dashboard approve/reject write API, so the Rejected column and drag-to-action need new backend support (Sign-off Readiness rows 9 and 10).
Customer Research, What We're Working Off
business_center
Ramp, Kanban for procurement approval pipelines open_in_new
Procurement/PO approval workflows are commonly visualised as Kanban boards with status columns, explicitly recommended for approval pipelines with SLA/overdue tracking; the Step 4 doc's net assessment calls Kanban "a near-exact match for the industry-standard approach", the direct basis for making it the default view. The item-age read and oldest-first ordering follow the Step 6 dossier's aging recommendation (approval queues in Tipalti, Bill.com and Planergy are aging, actionable lists) and Jo Lopez's design-sandbox purchasing build (age-descending sort); the empty-state copy is adapted from her build, with attribution.
Logic, What This Shows and Why We Built It This Way

Final build (2026-08-19, composed per the owner-confirmed sheet, per direct instruction). Built as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[13] (the purF block); the A/B/C branches stay untouched and reachable from the design-option switch above, with Final as the default. TAKEN FROM OPTION B: the Kanban board as the default view with a PO Table alternate. CHANGED FROM EVERY OPTION: the entire PO-status vocabulary is now the four confirmed real approval stages (Awaiting my approval next, Awaiting my approval, Unapproved, Approved), replacing the earlier invented Pending Approval / Approved / Overdue set and resolving the vocabulary conflict recorded in Final Check - Items Needing Your Review.md; Overdue is not a stage and not a column, it is a Table-only flag (red highlight plus a text flag, never colour alone). NEW: the dynamic Approval Path filter (populated from the orders matching the current status, disabled when only one path exists, per the old design); item age on every card with oldest-first ordering inside each column (owner sort decision this round, aging read per the Step 6 dossier and Jo's build); the PO record modal opened by card or row click (Detail, Approvals, Attachments, Note, Payment Approval tabs, matching today's Requests, Update screen; the live product navigates there, and the dossier's inline approve/reject overlay recommendation is recorded as deferred, not built); purposeful empty states ("Nothing needs your approval" when there is nothing at all, a filter-specific message when filters match nothing, quiet "None waiting" columns otherwise). DROPPED (owner decisions this round): the Status Donut view (was never built by any option) and the encumbrance chart (stays cut per the Step 4 doc). Department, Year and Overdue are Table-view-only filters, scoped per the Step 4 Filters table; all three remain unconfirmed backend fields rendered as if real per Rule 11, with the caveat in Widget_Specs. Data lives in standalone PURF_ constants next to WRENDER[13] (not MOCK_DATA, so mock-data.master.js needs no re-sync; the A/B/C mock series are untouched). Sizing follows Jo's three-size model (Glance, Explore, Detail; no Small, this widget's standing exception) via the generic fc-fmode mechanism, and the Glance card title reads the live "N awaiting my approval next" figure through the existing FC_KPI_HEADLINE plumbing. Known backend risks accepted by the owner this round and carried in Step 4: the Modern API only approximately reimplements the "Awaiting my approval next" sequence-chain check, and server-side filter persistence is not implemented yet. FC_VERSION[13] = 2.0. No em dashes in any user-facing string.

v2.6 (2026-08-19, owner design: the split Finish column). The board ends with a standing FINISH column split lengthwise: Close on top (accepts only paid, green cards) and Void below (accepts unpaid ones; paid orders cannot be voided from the dashboard, check reversal is an Accounts Payable flow). Dropping a card on either half opens a confirm popup with a reason; on confirm the card leaves the board. The two views deliberately have different jobs (owner decision): the Kanban is the live approval flow, showing only open or in-approval work, while the PO Table views everything over time, so its status filter gains Closed and Voided values (with the Year filter for the time window) and its "All statuses" includes the archive. Grounding: Closed (2) and Voided (3) were verified live this session as MANUAL statuses on the record screen's own Status dropdown, editable while a record is Unapproved and locked once Approved; the widget's queries only ever select statuses 0 and 1, so serving archived orders to the Table needs a new API ask (Sign-off Readiness row 13). Closed and voided records are final in the mock: the Approvals grid locks, payment history is read-only, and they can never return to the board.

v2.5 (2026-08-19, owner instruction: "I want the pop ups to have the same abilities as that page"). Built after a live click-through of beta1's Requests/Update screen for a real approved check request. The popup now mirrors that page: the header form (Vendor block with address and terms, Ship To, Email, Type, the record's own Status vocabulary (Unapproved / Approved / Closed / Voided), Approval Path editable while Pending, Payment Approval Path, Requisition or Check Request number and date, Issued To, Agent, Shipping, Date Requested); the Detail tab's line-item grid with Fund / Department / Account # and the Tax / Freight / Other / Total strip; the Approvals tab as the REAL grid (one "Ends with" row, Approved and Rejected checkboxes with a Reason field, Hold checkbox with its own Reason, Approval Updated By), fully interactive: ticking a box moves the card through the same guarded logic as dragging, so a held request refuses approval changes and a paid request is locked; the Attachments tab with an Add New Attachment stub; an editable Note plus the activity log; and the full Payment Approval tab (Add Invoice Payment Approval, the invoice grid with Check # / Check Date / Setup Information, the per-invoice account distribution, and the real Submit for Approval checkbox, which is what now marks the request paid and turns the card green). Every edit persists in-memory for the session. Backend note: all of these abilities need the write APIs already recorded in Sign-off Readiness rows 10-12; the live click-through also confirmed the record screen exposes Closed and Voided statuses that the widget never surfaces (kept out of scope).

v2.4 (2026-08-19, owner design round: colour-state cards, hold, and one-step payment entry). No new columns; the CARD COLOUR carries the sub-state, always paired with text. Payment simplifies to two states: an unpaid Approved card stays neutral with an amber "Payment: not paid" badge, and clicking it opens the record modal directly on its Payment Approval tab, where entering the invoice numbers and submitting turns the card GREEN with "Payment: paid" (one step per owner decision; on the real screen the paid signal is the check number and date being filled, so dev should treat green as check-issued). HOLD follows the code: the real Approvals tab carries a Hold checkbox with its own Reason per approval row (owner's live screenshot), so hold is available wherever something is still in progress, Pending and Approved-unpaid cards, never Paid or Rejected; whether the payment side has its own hold is not visible in the code trace and is recorded TO CONFIRM. Put on hold / Remove hold live in the record modal, each records a reason note; a held card turns YELLOW with a lock icon and its reason, and cannot be dragged until someone removes the hold (drag is blocked at dragstart and the move guard refuses held cards). One mock request ships held (PO-2891, "Waiting on budget confirmation") so the state demos. Colour legend: yellow = on hold, green = paid, red column = rejected; every colour is paired with its text label. New backend needs recorded in Step 4 (rows 11-12): payment status as a dashboard read field, and hold/remove-hold plus payment-entry write APIs.

v2.3 (2026-08-19, owner decision after the payment-approval code check). Payment approval is a SEPARATE workflow from order approval: invoice-level, on its own Payment Approval Path, with real data entry (invoice number, tax/freight/other, check number and date, GL account distributions, a per-invoice Submit for Approval), living only on the record screen; neither codebase serves any of it to the dashboard. Because a drag cannot enter invoice data, it is not an action here: Approved cards now carry a READ-ONLY payment-status badge (Payment: pending / submitted / paid), repeated in the record modal's Payment Approval tab, and the record screen stays where the actual payment work happens. The status field is Rule 11 forward-design (a new read API field, Sign-off Readiness row 11).

v2.2 (2026-08-19, owner correction, per direct instruction: "this is the approval process, this is how kanban should be"). The Kanban columns are now the approval STATES from the real record screen's Approvals tab: Pending, Approved, Rejected, replacing the four-stage column set built earlier the same day (that set was the status FILTER's vocabulary, not the approval process itself; it moves to the Step 4 doc's Design History). Cards are draggable between columns: dropping on a different column opens a Reason/note popup mirroring the real Approvals tab's Reason field, Confirm applies the move and records the note on the request (visible in the record modal's Note tab, and as the Reason on its Approvals tab for rejections), Cancel reverts. This supersedes the morning's "inline actioning deferred" decision: the Step 6 dossier's make-it-actionable recommendation (11.2) is now adopted in drag form. Two honest backend requirements recorded in Step 4 Sign-off Readiness: the legacy widget NEVER shows rejected orders (the Rejected column needs a data change) and no dashboard approve/reject write API exists yet (the dossier's own open question). Drag is pointer-only; the record modal remains the keyboard route, flagged under Accessibility. Two rejected mock requests were added so the Rejected column demos populated.

Quick-access shortcuts to common tasks for the current module and page — weighted toward actions that let the user add or input data (write a check, run payroll, enter a contribution), each one clearly labelled with its target module — supplemented by the user's own saved "My Tasks"/"My Reports" shortcuts.

Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Half 1 — Module Task Shortcuts. The Module dropdown (Large only, via the same generic inline-filter mechanism every other widget uses) picks which module's real task list renders, sourced from Step 1 Section 8's confirmed Label — URL data per module (MOCK_DATA.moduleTasks) — not invented. Each tile's icon is matched to the task's subject (journal, transaction, vendor, employee, invoice, etc.) per the icon-mapping table in Widget_Specs/W14-Main-Content-Tasks.md, so two different actions on the same kind of record share an icon.

Half 2 — My Tasks & My Reports. This is the existing legacy saved-shortcut feature (see reference screenshots, 2026-07-21) surfaced inside this widget instead of wherever it lives today — not new save/pin functionality. Saving still happens via the existing "Add To My Tasks" action elsewhere in the app; this panel only displays what's already saved. Both the existing side-panel instance and this widget instance are confirmed to work off the same underlying save mechanism simultaneously.

KPI size — added, frozen, then reopened for one more experiment, all 2026-07-21. There's still no natural headline number for a purely navigational shortcuts panel. Latest pass: Main Content Tasks, My Tasks, and My Reports icons all sit in one continuous, non-wrapping row (.w14-hscroll), separated by a vertical line (.w14-vline) between each group, scrollable left/right — the only way to fit three icon groups into a 300×110 card without shrinking or wrapping them. Only that one row scrolls; the card's chrome bar above it is untouched, exactly as it's always been. Change Module still works via the 3-dot "Change filters" modal.

Small — icon-only tiles kept, title and a vertical line added 2026-07-21. Half 1 is unchanged: the same compact icon-only row as KPI (first 4 tasks), per direct instruction ("keep the small icons") — now with a small label above it showing the active module's name, matching My Tasks/My Reports' own label style below (per direct instruction, to use the free space the card had left over). My Tasks and My Reports sit side by side below a thin divider, now separated from each other by a real vertical-line element (.w14-vline) rather than just a gap. Module is only changeable via the 3-dot "Change filters" modal.

Medium — reverted to the bigger tile, Half 2 added, then a scroll test 2026-07-21. Half 1 goes back to the original icon+label tile (w14BigTileGrid, same one Large uses) instead of the compact icon-only row, per direct instruction ("use the big Cards for the link like you had before the KPI card was added"). Half 2 uses the same two full labelled panels Large uses — deliberately not capped, so combined with an uncapped Half 1 there's more content than the card's fixed 240px height can hold. Explicit one-off experiment, per direct instruction, not a new standard: the card's chrome bar (title, refresh, eye, 3-dot menu) stays fixed and never scrolls, exactly as before; everything below it now scrolls internally with a slim custom scrollbar, via a selector scoped to only this one card (#fc-opt-14-m .opt-v). This deliberately deviates from Hard Rule 2 ("nothing scrolls except Expanded and table rows") — flagged in `General Widget Design Rules.md` and Widget_Specs/W14-Main-Content-Tasks.md as a test result, not something other widgets should copy without the same explicit sign-off.

Large — reverted to the bigger tile. Same change as Medium: Half 1 is back to w14BigTileGrid (icon+label, 4 per row, no cap) instead of the compact icon-only row it briefly used. Half 2 is unchanged — the full My Tasks/My Reports lists, as originally built.

Customer Research — What We're Working Off
business_center
Xero — Bank Reconciliation open_in_new
Bank-balance widgets should show real-time balances with clear cash-flow context; for nonprofits specifically, sources emphasise highlighting available unrestricted cash and how long it will last. The All Accounts comparison views (table/bar/cards) are all standard, interchangeable presentations for this data — the doc notes the Single Account breakdown (see flag below) rests on user need rather than competitive benchmarking, since it's a legacy-specific feature with no direct competitor confirmation either way.
Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Each card is one bank account — icon, name, balance, status, and note — the default All Accounts view. A Balance Table alternate is available via Switch View. Small shows the same cards trimmed to 2-3 accounts; Large adds a combined-balance total row.

Flag — Single Account mode isn't built. Per the doc, selecting a specific account in the Account filter should switch the entire widget into a different mode: a 7-row structural breakdown (Beginning Balance → Deposits → Voids → Checks → Withdrawals → EFT → Ending Balance) plus a 4-category bar chart — described as "the most significant view-switching behaviour of any widget on the dashboard." Today, selecting a specific account just re-filters the same All-Accounts-shaped cards/table/bars down to that one account — the same view, not a different mode. Building the real breakdown needs new transaction-category mock data and a new table template with a fixed structural row order, neither of which exist yet, so this is flagged rather than approximated.

Two safe fixes made: the missing KPI-size card was added (Total Balance across all bank accounts, read from the unfiltered account list so it stays fixed regardless of the Account filter, per the doc). And an invented "Show" filter (Balance+Reconciliation/Balance Only/Reconciliation Only) was removed — the doc says plainly it "didn't correspond to anything in the old design," and it was never read by the render anyway. Separately, the doc leaves reconciliation status badges as a genuinely open, not-yet-decided item for this widget (unlike W07, where the same concept was decisively cut) — the Status column/badges you'll see here are exactly that open item, not a defect.

Fix made — Small-size headline removed. The prior code showed a "Total balance" headline + a single account's card at Small, instead of the doc's plain "active view, 2-3 accounts." Falls through to the same card list every other size uses now, just capped to fewer accounts.

Logic — What This Shows, and Why We Built It This Way

Each card is one invoice — vendor, reference, due date, amount, and an overdue/on-time status. A Table alternate lists the same invoices with a Status column. Small shows the same cards capped to 3; Large adds a running total.

Flag — no option groups cards by urgency tier. The doc's View 1 is "Cards grouped by urgency — Overdue · Due This Week · Due This Month," immediately actionable as three visual sections. What's shown above is a flat, capped list of individual invoice cards (already narrowed by whichever Due Date filter is active) — not grouped into the three urgency sections the doc describes. Building real urgency-grouped sections is a layout change, not a cosmetic one, so it's flagged rather than approximated.

Flag — Aging Donut (View 2) isn't available in this option. Only Option B ("Aging Bar Chart") has a pie/donut view, and it's built around 30-day age bands (0-30/31-60/61-90/90+) rather than this widget's own three Due Date categories (Overdue Now/Due This Week/Due This Month) — a different bucketing scheme than the widget's own filter uses. Separately, Option B's donut is filtered by the Due Date selection today, but the doc says "the donut always shows all due dates regardless of the filter" — a real bug, noted here for whoever picks this back up, though not fixed since Option B isn't the option shown on this page.

Flag — Option C ("Vendor Breakdown") is the idea the doc explicitly didn't adopt. The doc's "What Got Cut" section says a by-vendor donut cut was "considered... but not adopted in this lock" and is "worth raising as a future enhancement, not built into this version" — yet Option C implements exactly that, fully live and selectable today.

Fixes made: the missing KPI card was added (Total AP Outstanding, across all due dates, per the doc). The Small-size "Overdue now" headline was removed, falling through to the same capped card list every other size uses. And Option A's default view was swapped from Table to Cards, matching the doc's "Due Date Cards (default)" — Table now needs an explicit switch instead of being the fallthrough, which was backwards before. (The three flags above describe the A/B/C options, kept for the record; the Final below supersedes them.)

Final build (2026-08-19, per direct instruction). Built as a new additive opt==='F' branch in WRENDER[16] (the apF block); the A/B/C branches stay untouched and reachable from the design-option switch above, with Final as the default. It is a 1-to-1 copy of Jo Lopez's Widget Container Demo Accounts Payable By Due Date v2 build (her ap block): her invoice set carried over verbatim in standalone APF_ constants next to WRENDER[16] (not MOCK_DATA, so mock-data.master.js needs no re-sync; the A/B/C mock series are untouched), 12 invoices totalling $35,711.25 anchored to her 23 Jul 2026 as-of date so her band populations reproduce exactly ($7,670.50 overdue across 3 invoices); her Glance card (Accounts payable scope chip, total payable, one red "$X overdue" or green "Nothing overdue" pill, values-as-text with a plain-language title); her two-row header (filter chips top-left, total + overdue pill below); her hero table (Vendor / Invoice / Due date / Amount, every column sortable, due-ascending default with date ties broken by larger amount first, a vendor search past 6 rows, a selection-labelled total footer, and a two-line due cell whose second line reads "Overdue by N days" in red with a warning glyph, "Due today", or "Due in N days"); her aging-band grouping under tinted subheaders with per-band counts and subtotals when the filter is All due dates, flattening when a band or specific date is picked; her due-date filter popover (All due dates with the grand total, a By aging section listing only non-empty bands, a By specific date section listing every distinct due date earliest-first with per-date totals and Overdue tags, and a search input past 8 distinct dates); her Detail layout (the same table beside a Cash requirements panel whose All-due-dates row and four band rows double as the due filter, with aria-hidden share mini-bars, "N invoices, X% of total" or a disabled "nothing due", and a Top vendors owed top-5 rollup flagging per-vendor overdue in red); her fetch model (a due-filter change is the only fetch in her build, an 800ms header-skeleton + 5 skeleton table rows with "Updating outstanding invoices...", while sort changes never show loading); and her "Nothing outstanding" empty state (short variant at Glance). NO charts, NO drill-through, NO timeline, exactly as her v2 dropped them. 2026-08-19, per direct instruction: Final built as a 1-to-1 copy of Jo's v2 ap block (aging bands + cash requirements, no charts, no drill-through); band math adopted from her build (overdue = past due, 0-7 week, 8-30 month, 31+ later), settling Sign-off Readiness row 4; drill-through not built, row 1 stays open with the experts. 2026-08-19, per direct instruction: due-date horizon picker added in the standard v2 chip pattern; unique to this widget, scopes cash requirements; overdue always included. The horizon chip sits next to the due-date chip (All outstanding default, Next 7 / 30 / 60 / 90 days) and scopes the working invoice set to invoices due on or before the anchor plus N days, with overdue invoices always included; every downstream figure (KPI total, overdue pill, bands, table, cash panel, top vendors, due-date popover contents, footer) computes from the horizon-scoped set; if the current due filter becomes empty or invalid under a new horizon it snaps back to All due dates (mirroring the Time Window Module's snap rule); a horizon change counts as a fetch with the same 800ms loading treatment. Wiring follows this file's loanF/purF convention (a delegated data-apf click listener behind APF_WIRED and body-mounted apf-scoped popovers), not Jo's shell dispatch. Sizing follows Jo's three-tier model via the same generic fc-fmode mechanism as W01-W13/W17 (no Small under Final; Glance / Explore / Detail wording, KPI = Glance, Explore = her wide, Detail = her xwide), and the Glance card title reads the live payables scope through the existing FC_KPI_HEADLINE plumbing ("Total Payables, ..."). FC_VERSION[16] = 2.0. No em dashes in any new user-facing string.

Purpose
Answers two questions at once: how is each gift and pledge campaign tracking against its Goal, and how much is still due. The Glance headline is overall Goal progress (Total Received against Total Goal, with the overall Progress percent), coloured by status (blue under 75 percent, amber 75 percent or more, green with a Goal Met badge at 100 percent or more). v1.2 (2026-08-24): the two views no longer overlap. Goal Progress is bars only, one per campaign with no table beneath, closest to goal first, and its legend carries the count in each status plus the overall remaining to goal. Summary Table is the table only, the live product's exact columns (Purpose (Campaign), Pledge Total, Pledge Due, Received, Due Remaining, Percent Due) with a totals row that sums the first four. Explore and Detail now show ONE view at a time and differ by card size alone; the separate goal panel that used to sit beside the Detail table is gone, because the overall goal read belongs on the Glance card and appeared twice. Rollback: set GPF_V12_LAYOUT to false to restore the previous arrangement exactly. Every campaign row in the Summary Table expands to a per-donor breakdown, each donor pledge paced on its own begin to end term, sorted most behind pace first and paginated 20 per page (the Remittance Pledges drill). Pledge Due is per-pledge term proration (full once past a pledge's end date); Received counts gifts dated on or before the range end; Due Remaining is Pledge Due minus Received (over-received shows in parentheses, treated as favourable); Percent Due is Due Remaining over Pledge Due, the share still outstanding. Filters are Campaign and a date range (This year, Last 30 days, Custom), the range end acting as the as-of cutoff. Derived from the W04 Remittance Pledges Final; the campaign Goal is a modern field mocked for this build (see Widget_Specs).
